title: 第十二章　从改革到崩溃，1989—1991

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫并不
en: Gorbachev doesn’t

zh: 1989年3月，人民代表大会选举就是在危机从边疆地区悄悄蔓延的背景下举行的——这是1918年以来俄罗斯第一次真正的选举。这些选举，尤其是6月代表大会本身的首次会议，标志着戈尔巴乔夫时代的决定性转折点，即从共产主义的改组转向其积极瓦解的时刻。的确，1989年6月是全世界共产主义的伟大转折点：那个月的波兰选举启动了整个东欧体系的崩溃，北京天安门广场的屠杀则表明，即使在经济繁荣条件下，共产主义“制度内”改革也有其限度。到1989年底，柏林墙倒塌、所有东欧政权崩溃之后，已经越来越清楚，这个制度唯一的选择要么是和平的自我清算，要么是一场代价高昂但仍属暂时的守成行动。
en: It was against the background of crisis creeping in from the borderlands that the elections to the Congress of People’s Deputies took place in March 1989—the first real elections in Russia since 1918. These elections, and even more the first meeting of the Congress itself in June, marked the decisive turning point of the Gorbachev era, the moment of transition from the restructuring of Communism to its active disintegration. Indeed, June 1989 was the great turning point for Communism throughout the world: the Polish elections of that month started the collapse of the system throughout Eastern Europe, and the Tiananmen Square massacre in Beijing demonstrated the limits of “within-system” reform of Communism even under conditions of economic prosperity. By the end of 1989, after the fall of the Berlin Wall and the collapse of all the Eastern European regimes, it was becoming clear that the only alternatives for the system were either peaceful self-liquidation or a costly but still temporary holding operation.

zh: 民主化
en: DEMOCRATIZATION

zh: 1989年的第一次冲击是春天的苏联选举。它们是在一个从1917年重新启用、本只作修辞之用的口号下组织的——“一切权力归苏维埃”——但让戈尔巴乔夫吃惊的是，自由派把这个口号当真了，试图从党、从戈尔巴乔夫手中夺取真正的权力。而他们这样做，尽管选举制度的设计本是为了产生一个稳妥地支持总书记所设想的改革派“人民阵线”的代表大会。虽然代表大会及其最高苏维埃形式上拥有制宪和立法权力，实际上它们更像一个两级的咨询性议会，与其说为了治理，不如说为了向政府决策提供意见。
en: The first shock of 1989 was the Soviet elections in the spring. They had been organized under the slogan-resurrected from 1917 and intended only rhetorically—“all power to the soviets,” but the surprise for Gorbachev was that the liberals took this slogan literally and sought to wrest real power from the Party, and from Gorbachev. And they did this despite the fact that the electoral system had been constructed to yield a Congress safely devoted to the General Secretary’s concept of Popular Fronts loyal to

. Although the Congress and its Supreme Soviet formally had both constituent and legislative powers, in fact they resembled a two-tier consultative assembly designed less to govern than to provide input into the government’s policy making.

zh: 选举不是基于普选权，而是通过一种让人想起旧制度的复杂制度进行的，旨在钝化民主的效果。这使人们容易批评新制度只是政权持续极权性质的伪装；当时的苏联自由派正是这样批评“戈尔巴乔夫宪法”的。不过应当指出，这是1918年以来俄罗斯的任何形式的第一次选举，而从极权主义立即跃入成熟的普选民主，可能会危险地破坏稳定。此外，在1915年之前的那个世纪里，所有走向政治民主的欧洲国家都是分阶段完成的。这似乎就是戈尔巴乔夫及其助手的推理：“民主化”如同经济自由化一样，必须以“一步一步”、经校准的方式推进，以免吓坏机关使其公开反对，并让人民逐渐参与新方式。所有这一切都相当站得住脚。
en: The elections were conducted not on the basis of universal suffrage but by a complicated system, reminiscent of an Old Regime, intended to blunt the effect of democracy. This made it easy to criticize the new system as a mere camouflage of the continuing totalitarian nature of the regime; and the “Gorbachev Constitution” was so criticized at the time by Soviet liberals. Still, it should be pointed out that these were the first elections of any kind in Russia since 1918, and that an immediate leap from totalitarianism into full-fledged universal suffrage democracy could have been dangerously destabilizing. Moreover, all other European countries that had moved to political democracy in the century before 1915 had done so by stages. This, it seems, was the reasoning of Gorbachev and his aides: “democratization,” like economic liberalization, would have to proceed in a “step by step,” calibrated fashion, so as to not frighten the apparat into open opposition and to involve the people gradually in the new ways. And all of this was quite defensible.

children: 〔译注〕苏联在1918年之后也举行过多次最高苏维埃和地方苏维埃选举；1989年选举的变化在于部分席位引入了候选人竞争，而非此后首次举行任何形式的选举。
〔译注〕苏联在1918年之后也举行过多次最高苏维埃和地方苏维埃选举；1989年选举的变化在于部分席位引入了候选人竞争，而非此后首次举行任何形式的选举。

zh: 新政治制度的真正缺陷在别处。与经济改革一样，戈尔巴乔夫对自己的政治改革的
没有清晰概念，因为他的目标不是民主，正如不是市场：而是某种未加规定的民众参与和法治程度，与（据称已革新的）党的持续霸权相结合。但真正的民主与市场一样，都不需要这样的党。因此，戈尔巴乔夫的勇敢举措实际上是改革共产主义反复出现的“内部矛盾”的终极版本。
en: The real flaw of the new political system lay elsewhere. As with economic reform, Gorbachev had no clear idea of the

of his political reform, for his goal was not democracy any more than it was the market: it was, rather, an unspecified measure of popular participation and the rule of law in combination with the continuing hegemony of the (putatively regenerated) Party. But real democracy has no more need for such a Party than does a market. Thus Gorbachev’s bold initiative was in fact the ultimate version of the recurring “internal contradictions” of Reform Communism.

zh: 在戈尔巴乔夫宪法中，首先有两个议会，而不是一个。较大的代表大会（显然模仿雅典民众大会，即 Ecclesia）由民众和各“社会组织”直接选举产生。它由2250名成员组成，规模太大，无法成为议事机构。因此，它每年只开两三次短会，其主要职能是选举真正的政府机关：其主席团主席（“总统”）和实际的立法机构——一个由542名成员组成、全年开会的两院制最高苏维埃（相当于雅典的五百人议事会，即小型议事会）。随着立法机构这样间接选举产生，而总统或其副手实际主持两个机构，出现重大反对政府意志的机会微乎其微。
en: In the Gorbachev Constitution there were, first of all, two assemblies, not one. The larger Congress (apparently modelled on the Ecclesia, the Athenian popular Assembly) was directly elected by the population and various “social organizations.” Composed of 2,250 members, it was too large to be a deliberative body. It was, therefore, to meet only two or three times a year for short periods, and its main function was to elect the real governmental organs: the chairman of its Presidium (the “president”) and the actual legislature, a bicameral Supreme Soviet of 542 members that would meet throughout the year (the equivalent of the Athenian Boulé, or small Council). With this indirect election of the legislature, and with the president, or his deputy, actually presiding over both bodies, there was little chance of significant opposition to the government’s will.

children: 〔译注〕大会选举的是最高苏维埃及其主席；戈尔巴乔夫此前担任最高苏维埃主席团主席，1990年成为苏联总统，几个职务不可混同。
〔译注〕大会选举的是最高苏维埃及其主席；戈尔巴乔夫此前担任最高苏维埃主席团主席，1990年成为苏联总统，几个职务不可混同。

zh: 对自发民主的第二个限制是选举过程本身。750名代表大会代表由党、共青团和科学院等“社会组织”选举产生；人们假定党实际上会选定所有这些代表。而在为党保留的100个席位中，恰好提名了100名候选人，包括戈尔巴乔夫和大多数高级官员；这意味着领导层中没有一人需要在党内冒竞争选举的风险。其余三分之二代表在地区或民族选区选举产生；但即使在这些选区，地方党委书记也往往指定代表或自己参选。因此，当选代表的85%是党员。此外，还有通过一系列所谓“过滤器”的严格预选。首先，候选人必须由若干公民提出；其次，他或她的提名必须在不少于该选区500名居民的会议上获得批准，而当局很容易操纵这种集会；最后，候选人资格必须由选举委员会正式登记，党同样可以在那里干预。结果，384个选区的选票上只有一个名字——无例外地是一名党务官员的名字。
en: The second restraint on spontaneous democracy was the electoral process itself. Seven hundred fifty Congress deputies were elected by such “social organizations” as the Party, the Komsomol, and the Academy of Sciences; it was assumed that the Party would in fact select all of these deputies. And for the one hundred seats reserved for the Party, exactly one hundred candidates were nominated, including Gorbachev and most senior officials; this meant that no member of the leadership had to risk competitive election even within the Party. The remaining two thirds of the deputies were elected in territorial or national districts; but even in these constituencies the local Party secretary more often than not selected a deputy or stood for election himself. Thus, 85 percent of the elected deputies were Party members. Furthermore, there was a rigorous preselection of candidates through a series of “filters,” as these obstacles were called. First, a candidate had to be put forth by a number of citizens; second, his or her nomination had to be approved at a meeting of no fewer than five hundred residents of the district, and the authorities could easily stack such a gathering; finally, the candidacy had to be formally registered by an electoral commission, where again the Party could intervene. As a result, 384 districts had only one name—invariably that of a Party official—on their ballot.

zh: 尽管如此，仍有挑战制度的手段。首先是全国电视。过去两年撰写公开性重要文章的大多数人，在1988年底组成了一个政治俱乐部——莫斯科论坛，其中许多人现在是候选人。早在选举之前，他们就经常接受教育节目《奥斯坦金诺的相遇》采访；竞选开始后，他们开始出现在更受欢迎、更活跃的深夜节目《观点》上。然后还有更直接的鼓动形式：当科学院的过滤器运作得如此之好，以致萨哈罗夫未能获得提名时，舆论哗然，党再次干预，把他列入选票。在拥有相当多受教育人口的大城市，自由派为其候选人和反对机关候选人组织了良好的竞选活动；在列宁格勒，“选举89”团体在地铁站散发传单，借用政府车辆作为宣传车，并说服多数人在选票上划掉无人竞争的当地第一书记兼政治局候补委员的名字，从而策划了他的失败。类似策略在斯维尔德洛夫斯克、符拉迪沃斯托克、伏尔加格勒、明斯克、基辅和利沃夫等主要中心也使选举结果发生了类似逆转。当然，在波罗的海国家，结果更为激进：人民阵线拿下三分之二席位，官方候选人只有获得阵线批准才能当选。（在高加索各共和国，日益严重的公共骚乱阻止了正常选举——因而也阻止了任何激进突破——而中亚各共和国公民则按党老板的吩咐投票。）
en: Nonetheless, there were means of challenging the system. The first of these was national television. Most of the people who had been writing the great articles of

during the two previous years had, in late 1988, formed a political club, the Moscow Tribune, and many of these individuals were now candidates. Well before the elections they had been regularly interviewed on the educational program
; once the campaign started, they began to appear on the more popular and lively late-night show

. And then there were more direct forms of agitation: when the filters of the Academy worked so well that Sakharov failed to be nominated, there was such an outcry that the Party intervened again to put him on the ballot. In large cities with a sizeable educated population, liberal elements mounted well-organized campaigns for their own candidates and against those of the apparat; in Leningrad, the group “Elections 89” passed out leaflets at subway stations, borrowed government vehicles to use as sound trucks, and orchestrated the defeat of the local First Secretary and alternate Politburo member, who was running unopposed, by persuading a majority to cross his name off the ballot. And similar tactics produced similar upsets in such major centers as Sverdlovsk, Vladivostok, Volgograd, Minsk, Kiev, and Lvov. In the Baltic states, of course, the results were even more radical: the Popular Fronts took two thirds of the seats, while official candidates survived only if they had a Front’s approval. (In the Caucasian republics growing public disorder prevented normal elections—and hence any radical breakthrough—while citizens of the Central Asian republics voted as the Party bosses told them to.)

zh: 但最具震撼性的选举逆转发生在莫斯科。在那里，在一个全城特别选区，鲍里斯·叶利钦获得约500万票，占总票数的90%，击败了官方候选人——一位工厂厂长（该市第一书记不敢参选）。此外，叶利钦的竞选纲领反对党的特权和权力，主张直接选举新总统并建立多党制；其他自由派都没有如此明确地说出他们的真实目标。
en: But the most momentous upset occurred in Moscow, There, in a special city-wide constituency, Boris Yeltsin received some five million votes, or 90 percent of the total, against the official candidate, a factory director (the city’s First Secretary did not dare to stand). Yeltsin, moreover, had campaigned against Party privilege and power and in favor of direct election of the new president and the creation of a multiparty system; none of the other liberals had been so explicit in stating their real aims.

zh: 选举的总体结果是，戈尔巴乔夫获得了一个愿意不加质疑追随他的多数——但自由派拿下了约300个席位。虽然这些自由派大多在形式上仍是党员，但他们不是来自机关，而且党员身份现在的意义已远不如前。此外，从2月竞选开始到5月最后决选期间，边疆地区的革命终于抵达以斯拉夫人为主的中心地区。大城市已经政治化，尽管省级中心和农村直到政权终结、甚至之后仍大体处于机关控制之下。改革以前只是党的领导层的事务，现在成了整个社会的事务。人们第一次感到自己能够为自己的命运做点什么，而他们最想做的事，就是拒绝党的霸权。这才是选举、尤其是叶利钦胜利的真正意义，而不是正式多数的规模。
en: The overall result of the election was that Gorbachev obtained a large majority willing to follow his lead without question—but the liberals took about three hundred seats. Although most of these liberals were formally Party members, they were not from the apparat, and besides, Party membership now meant much less than before. Furthermore, between the opening of the campaign in February and the final runoffs in May, the revolution of the borderlands at last reached the central Slavic areas. The larger cities had become politicized, though provincial centers and the countryside would remain largely under the control of the apparat until the end of the regime, and even after.

, previously the business of only the Party leadership, now became a matter for society at large. People for the first time felt they could actually do something about their lot, and the most important thing they wanted to do was to reject the hegemony of the Party. This, not the size of the formal majority, was the true significance of the election, and especially of Yeltsin’s triumph.

zh: 尽管如此，仍非常需要谨慎。机关在每一道“过滤器”上都奋力作战。4月出现了其他与一年前安德烈耶娃信相当的惊吓。如前一章所述，军队向第比利斯的民族主义示威者开枪，显然得到政治局纵容；同一周，里加街头出现了坦克。此外，一项限制性极强的法律修订正在准备中，透着不祥气息。利加乔夫和保守派是否在准备镇压以取消选举结果？戈尔巴乔夫本人是否对自己所允许的事情产生了疑虑？于是，代表大会在5月底开会，气氛中希望夹杂着不祥的预感。
en: Nonetheless, caution was still very much in order. The apparat had fought hard at every “filter.” In April there were other scares comparable to the Andreeva letter of a year earlier. As was mentioned in the previous chapter, the army fired on nationalist demonstrators in Tbilisi, apparently with Politburo connivance; and in that same week tanks were seen in the streets of Riga. Moreover, an ominously restrictive revision of the legal code was in preparation. Were Ligachev and the conservatives preparing a crackdown to annul the results of the elections? Might Gorbachev himself be having second thoughts about what he had permitted? So the Congress met at the end of May in an atmosphere in which hope was tempered by foreboding.

〔译注〕关于1989年4月9日第比利斯镇压，调查记录涉及工兵铲、化学剂和踩踏等；本段所说军队向示威者开枪的具体情况尚未得到所查证据证实。

zh: 经过一番犹豫，戈尔巴乔夫决定会议进行全国电视直播。按照人民阵线战略，他的代表大会议程要求在他的报告之后立即选举总统和最高苏维埃。但自由派有更大胆的想法：1989年是法国大革命两百周年，一些代表半开玩笑地把代表大会称为三级会议，把新的最高苏维埃称为杜马。撇开这些比较，他们确实想与戈尔巴乔夫分享权力，而不只是发挥咨询作用。因此，他们的议程要求在他的报告之后进行彻底辩论，只有在这场讨论之后，代表大会才选举总统和最高苏维埃——这种安排意味着戈尔巴乔夫依赖于新当选的“人民代表”。但就在代表大会召开前，戈尔巴乔夫及其首席助手阿纳托利·卢基扬诺夫秘密会见了当时所谓的自由派“莫斯科小组”，“对他们施压”，以扼杀这一异见方案。
en: After some hesitation, Gorbachev decided that the proceedings would be televised live and nationally. In accordance with the strategy of the Popular Front, his agenda for the Congress called for his report to be followed immediately by the election of the president and the Supreme Soviet. But the liberals had bolder ideas: 1989 was the two-hundredth anniversary of the French Revolution, and some of the deputies, only half-jokingly, spoke of the Congress as the Estates General, and of the new Supreme Soviet as the Duma. Such comparisons aside, they did in fact want power sharing with Gorbachev and not just a consultative role. Accordingly, their agenda called for his report to be followed by a thorough debate, and only after this discussion would the Congress elect the president and the Supreme Soviet—an arrangement that implied Gorbachev’s dependence on the newly elected “deputies of the people.” But just before the Congress convened, Gorbachev and his chief aide, Anatolii Lukianov, met confidentially with the Moscow Group, as the liberals then were called, and “worked them over” to squelch this dissident scenario.

zh: 于是，代表大会按戈尔巴乔夫的脚本进行，但更激进的自由派不断发动批评战。戈尔巴乔夫如期当选总统，代表大会选出的最高苏维埃如此传统，其中没有一名莫斯科自由派。（这太尴尬了，以致说服一名代表辞职，为叶利钦腾出位置。）阿法纳西耶夫愤慨地把新议会称为“斯大林-勃列日涅夫式”机构，并谴责代表大会“咄咄逼人的顺从多数”，走廊里很快传开消息，说失败的自由派少数即将发表一份“宣言”。随着日子一天天过去，一个接一个发言者抨击制度的某种弊端：经济效率低下；国家普遍贫困；党腐败；医院没有热水、医疗没有药品的丑闻；教育不足；军队在阿富汗和格鲁吉亚的不当行为；最后，在一次令人震惊的发言中，克格勃作为行使“对社会全面控制”的“地下帝国”的角色。
en: So the Congress followed Gorbachev’s script, but not without a running war of criticism from the more militant liberals. Gorbachev was duly elected president, and the Congress chose a Supreme Soviet so traditional that it contained not a single Moscow liberal. (This was so embarrassing that one deputy was prevailed on to resign in order to make room for Yeltsin.) Afanasiev indignantly called the new parliament a “Stalinist-Brezhnevite” body and denounced the “aggressively submissive majority” of the Congress, and word soon spread in the corridors that a “declaration” from the defeated liberal minority would soon be forthcoming. As the days went by, speaker after speaker attacked one or another vice of the system: the inefficiency of the economy; the widespread poverty of the country; the corruption of the Party; the scandal of hospitals without running hot water and health care without medicines; the inadequacies of education; the misconduct of the army in Afghanistan and Georgia; and finally, in one astounding outburst, the role of the KGB as an “underground empire” exercising “comprehensive control over society.”

zh: 然而，异见派没有发表共同宣言，人们推测任何要求宣读此类文件的请求都会被主席即戈尔巴乔夫拒绝。然后，在最后一天，一位年轻代表说出“宣言”一词，果然立即被打断。然而，他原来是个诱饵，因为已经发言八次的萨哈罗夫立即再次要求发言。戈尔巴乔夫害怕萨哈罗夫可能说什么，但更害怕拒绝他的后果，于是给了这位执着的“安德烈·德米特里耶维奇”五分钟，萨哈罗夫随即宣读了一份他称为“权力法令”的东西。（他使用“法令”这个具有革命仪式感的词，因为列宁1917年10月关于土地与和平的“法令”用过它。）萨哈罗夫“法令”的实质是，应废除规定党“领导和指导作用”的宪法第六条，全部权力应转归苏维埃及其代表大会，而党在1917年正是从那里夺取了权力。至此，“改革”制度问题的核心——权力问题——终于被点名，而且是在全国面前。萨哈罗夫尚未说完，戈尔巴乔夫就掐断了麦克风，但电视摄像机仍在拍摄。从此，萨哈罗夫公开提出的问题再也无法回避。
en: Still, no general declaration was produced by the dissidents, and the presumption was that any request to read such a document would be refused by the chair, that is, by Gorbachev. Then, on the last day, one young deputy pronounced the word “declaration” and was indeed promptly cut off. He turned out to have been a decoy, however, as Sakharov, who had already spoken eight times, immediately asked for the floor once again. Gorbachev was afraid of what Sakharov might say, but he was even more afraid of the consequences of turning him down, so he granted the persistent “Andrei Dmitrievich” five minutes, and Sakharov proceeded to read something he called a “Decree on Power.” (He used the ceremonially revolutionary word “decree” because Lenin had used it in his “Decrees,” on Land and Peace, in October 1917.) The substance of Sakharov’s “Decree” was that Article 6 of the Constitution, establishing the “leading and guiding role of the Party,” should be abrogated, and that all power should pass to the soviets and their Congress, from which the Party had seized it in 1917. Here the nub of the problem of “reforming” the system—the question of power—was at last named, and, in front of the whole country. Gorbachev cut off the microphone before Sakharov had finished, but the television camera remained on. Henceforth there would be no avoiding the problem Sakharov had brought out into the open.

zh: 当为期十二天的代表大会结束时，苏联已是一个新国家。公开性开始的使制度去神圣化的工作，现在完成了。千百万人听到自己的私下想法被公开说出；个人看到自己在制度小角落里观察到的弊端是整个联盟共有的。现在每个人都知道，可以说最大胆的话而不必担心报复。公众对代表大会的兴趣如此强烈，以致在会议电视转播期间工业生产下降了20%。正如一位自由派代表总结的：“[代表大会]的主要成就是祛除了苏联权力的神秘性。”
en: When the twelve days of the Congress were finished, the Soviet Union was a new country. The work of desacralizing the system, begun by

, was now completed. Millions of people had heard their private thoughts uttered in public; individuals saw that the evils they had observed in their own little corner of the system were common to the whole Union. And everyone now knew it was possible to say the boldest things without fear of retribution. So intense was the public’s interest in the Congress that industrial production dropped 20 percent during the televised coverage of the proceedings. As one liberal deputy summed it up: “The main achievement [of the Congress] was the demystification of Soviet power.”

zh: 但国家也留下了一种强烈的不完整感：正如另一位代表所说，“这么多事实，却没有结论。”

而政府确实没有提出变革纲领，同时国内局势明显恶化。代表大会期间发生了两起灾难：在西伯利亚，一条管道泄漏丁烷气，由于“犯罪性疏忽”，气体被一列经过的火车点燃，引发爆炸，造成约450人死亡；几乎同时，乌兹别克斯坦费尔干纳谷地发生针对麦斯赫特土耳其少数民族的屠杀，造成数十人伤亡。两起事件合在一起，既戏剧化了苏联工业成就的脆弱，也戏剧化了多民族联盟的脆弱。与此同时，所有人的生活水平现在都明显下降。国家似乎陷入漂流，政府陷入无能。
en: But the country was also left with a great feeling of incompleteness: As another deputy put it, “so many facts, and no conclusions.”

And indeed the government offered no program for change, while at the same time the situation in the country was visibly deteriorating. During the Congress there had been two disasters: in Siberia, butane gas had leaked from a pipeline, and through an act of “criminal negligence” it caught fire from a passing train, producing an explosion that killed some 450 persons; almost simultaneously, in the Fergana Valley of Uzbekistan a pogrom against the Meskhetian Turkic minority claimed dozens of victims. The two incidents together dramatized the fragility of both the Soviet industrial achievement and the multinational Union. At the same time, living standards for everyone were now visibly declining. The country seemed caught in drift, and the government mired in impotence.

〔译注〕这起事故发生在巴什基尔地区乌法附近，泄漏气体爆炸波及两列相向列车，而非西伯利亚的一列火车；早期和后来的死亡统计数字亦不相同。

zh: 7月，民众开始自己采取行动。库兹涅茨克盆地的矿工罢工，要求提高工资，并提供食品和……肥皂。运动很快蔓延到顿巴斯和北方沃尔库塔的矿山，那里增加了一项政治要求：废除第六条，结束党的领导作用。戈尔巴乔夫和政府匆忙接过矿工的事业，同意他们的经济要求；毕竟，是他号召人民参与改革的，而且政府没有煤炭储备。此外，铁路工人威胁罢工，这一可怕的可能性必须不惜一切代价加以避免。
en: In July the population started taking matters into its own hands. The miners of the Kuznetsk Basin went on strike for higher wages, food and … soap. Soon the movement spread to the Donbas and the mines of Vorkuta in the north, where a political demand was added: abrogation of Article 6 and the end of the Party’s leading role. Gorbachev and the government hastily took up the miners’ cause and acceded to their economic demands; he had, after all, summoned the people to become involved in
, and the government, moreover, had no reserves of coal. In addition, the railroad workers were threatening to strike, and that dire eventuality had to be headed off at all costs.

zh: 与此同时，在莫斯科，约250名自由派代表——他们正是在代表大会期间才相互认识的——组成了一个名为跨地区集团的议会党团。其主要领导人是萨哈罗夫、叶利钦、阿法纳西耶夫和波波夫。他们的目标是实现代表大会第一次会议未能完成的事：把真正的权力从戈尔巴乔夫转移到最高苏维埃。为此，他们寻求与新觉醒的工人以及少数民族、特别是波罗的海人的主权运动结成联盟。他们的具体纲领是结束党的领导作用，引入多党制、私有财产和市场经济。为实施这一纲领，他们期待在定于来年举行的地方苏维埃选举中夺取权力。公开性尚未充分到可以在印刷品上陈述这些目标，但小组成员私下里自由谈论它们。
en: Meanwhile, back in Moscow some two hundred fifty liberal deputies, who had come to know each other only as a result of the Congress, formed a caucus called the Inter-Regional Group. Its principal leaders were Sakharov, Yeltsin, Afanasiev, and Popov. Their aim was to achieve what the first session of the Congress had failed to accomplish: a transfer of real power from Gorbachev to the Supreme Soviet. To this end they sought to form an alliance with the newly awakened workers as well as with the sovereignty movement among the national minorities, particularly the Baits. Their concrete program was to end the Party’s leading role and to introduce a multiparty system, private property, and a market economy. To implement this program, they were expecting to take power through the local soviet elections scheduled for the coming year.
was not yet so complete that these aims could be stated in print, but the members of the group talked about them freely in private.

zh: 然而，在西部边疆地区，激进主义现在公开表达：8月23日，《莫洛托夫-里宾特洛甫条约》五十周年，一百万人组成人链，横跨三个波罗的海国家，从塔林到维尔纽斯。乌克兰现在也围绕“鲁赫”组织动员起来；1990年1月，它模仿波罗的海国家的示威，组织了自己的人链，从利沃夫经基辅直到波尔塔瓦。到夏末，全国大部分地区已存在近似“双重权力”的局面。正如鲁赫一位领导人总结代表大会后的局势：“国家现在站在十字路口。从这里，我们要么走中国道路，要么走波兰—匈牙利道路。”
en: In the western borderlands, however, radicalism was now openly expressed: on August 23, the fiftieth anniversary of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, a human chain of a million people was formed across the three Baltic states from Tallinn to Vilnius. Ukraine, too, was now mobilized for action around the organization Rukh, which in January 1990 imitated the demonstration in the Baltic states with a human chain of its own from Lvov through Kiev and on to Poltava. By the end of the summer something approximating “dual power” existed throughout much of the country. As one leader of Rukh summed up the post-Congress situation: “The country now stands at a crossroads. From here, we either go the Chinese way or the Polish-Hungarian way.”

zh: 改革的动力促成了各地列宁主义制度的危机，而国外改革共产主义的波折又反过来作用于苏联中心。按时间顺序，第一次外来冲击来自中国，并不是因为苏联当时直接参与中国事务，而是因为如此巨大的社会主义体系中的变化只能对原初模式构成挑战。正是中国以邓小平1978年的经济自由化开启了改革共产主义的第二轮伟大浪潮。直到1989年，中国的巨大成功增加了苏联人改革的压力；天安门广场屠杀之后，中国成了改革陷阱的警示案例；而在这两个阶段，中国道路都首次在两国关系中为昔日的“老大哥”指明了未来方向。
en: The impetus of

had contributed to a crisis of Leninist systems everywhere, and the vicissitudes of Reform Communism abroad reacted in turn on the Soviet center. In point of time the first foreign impact came from China, not because of any current Soviet connection with Chinese affairs, but because change in so huge a socialist system could only provide a challenge for the original model. It was China that had inaugurated the second great round of Reform Communism with Deng Xiaoping’s economic liberalization of 1978. Down to 1989, China’s great success had contributed to the pressure on the Soviets to reform; after the Tiananmen Square massacre, China became a cautionary example of the pitfalls of reform; and in both phases, the Chinese path pointed the way to the future for the erstwhile “elder brother” for the first time in their relationship.

zh: 变化始于1975年毛泽东去世。在国内，这一事件使清算“伟大舵手”的硬共产主义、启动邓小平的软共产主义成为可能，后者是威权政府与市场自由的结合。对外，毛泽东的离去结束了1963年分裂以来中苏关系的激烈敌意。尽管仍存在重要的地区利益冲突，但争夺国际社会主义领导权的旧怨对双方都逐渐失去意义。
en: The change began with Mao Zedong’s death in 1975. Internally, this event made it possible to liquidate the hard Communism of the Great Helmsman and to launch the soft Communism of Deng, a combination of authoritarian government with market freedom. Externally, Mao’s departure ended the intense animosity that had characterized Sino-Soviet relations since the split in 1963. Although important regional conflicts of interest remained, the old feud for leadership of international socialism gradually lost its meaning for both sides.

〔译注〕毛泽东逝世于1976年9月9日，而非原书所写的1975年。

zh: 因此，戈尔巴乔夫掌权后，同这个兄弟“社会主义”国家实现关系正常化。因为戈尔巴乔夫比中国更需要这种和解，他不得不像与西方和解时那样，作出所有让步。于是苏联不得不同意撤出阿富汗、削减中苏边境兵力，并迫使盟友越南撤离柬埔寨。正是这种东方政策最终把戈尔巴乔夫带到北京，时在1989年5月，恰在苏联人民代表大会前夕。虽然这一新政策没有给他带来任何实际收获，但访问的时机凸显了中国局势中与国内及东欧局势最相关的一面。
en: Therefore, after Gorbachev came to power, he normalized relations with the Chinese as a fraternal “socialist” state. Because Gorbachev needed this rapprochement more than the Chinese did, he had to proceed, as in his rapprochement with the West, by making all of the concessions. Thus the Soviets had to agree to withdraw from Afghanistan, reduce their forces on the Sino-Soviet border, and force their ally Vietnam to evacuate Cambodia. It was this

that finally brought Gorbachev to Beijing in May 1989, on the very eve of the Soviet Congress of People’s Deputies. Although this new policy netted him nothing, the timing of his visit served to highlight an aspect of the Chinese situation most relevant to the situation at home and in Eastern Europe.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫抵达北京时，中国版的改革共产主义正达到其重大危机。要求民主的学生已经占领天安门广场，而改革的榜样是鼓励他们采取行动的一个促成因素。但对苏联集团来说，中国危机的更深含义在别处。戈尔巴乔夫以政治开始改革，邓小平则相反，以经济开始改革。然而到1989年，两者都陷入僵局，因为一种改革没有另一种改革，会破坏整个制度的稳定。的确，戈尔巴乔夫告诉东道主，经济改革没有相应的彻底政治变革行不通；在那种情况下，这等于建议不要镇压学生。然而在党国的总体制度中，反过来同样正确，苏联将在1991年发现这一点。这就提出了改革末期俄罗斯争论激烈的一个问题：戈尔巴乔夫把经济改革置于政治民主化之前是否会更好？实际上他没有那个选择，只要简要比较苏联和中国的条件便可明白。
en: Gorbachev arrived in Beijing just as the Chinese version of Reform Communism was reaching its great crisis. The Students for Democracy were already occupying Tiananmen Square, and the example of

was a contributory factor in emboldening them to act. But for the Soviet bloc the deeper meaning of the Chinese crisis lay elsewhere. Whereas Gorbachev had begun his reform with politics, Deng Xiaoping had pursued the opposite course by starting his reform with economics. Yet by 1989 both had arrived at an impasse because one kind of reform without the other destabilized the system as a whole. Indeed, Gorbachev told his hosts that economic reform without a correspondingly thorough political change would not work, and under the circumstances this amounted to advice not to crack down on the students. Yet in the total system of the Party-state the reverse was just as true, as the Soviet Union would discover in 1991. And this raises a question much debated in Russia at the end of

: would Gorbachev have done better to put economic reform ahead of political democratization? In reality he did not have that choice, as a brief comparison of Soviet and Chinese conditions readily reveals.

〔译注〕戈尔巴乔夫1985年上台后首先提出经济“加速”及相关政策，政治改革随后逐步深化；作者此处的概括应结合前章时间线理解。

zh: 1979年邓小平开始改革时，中国80%的人口在农村。因此，仅仅放松公社制度、让农民自由生产，大多数人口就能经历繁荣的大扩张，整个经济在十年间就能出现每年约10%至15%的增长浪潮。相比之下，在苏联，集体化的毁灭性后果和庞大的农业官僚机构排除了任何这样的快速经济好转。此外，斯大林曾是一个“成功者”，就创建庞大工业设施和建设超级大国而言；毛泽东则是一个失败的国家建设者，其疯狂的大跃进和愚蠢的文化大革命。因此，戈尔巴乔夫不得不清算他的国家视为荣耀的许多东西；邓小平只需克服大多数国人想要摆脱的政策。因此，戈尔巴乔夫不得不通过“民主化”改组国家的行政结构，缓慢而间接地推进；邓小平则可以保持其政治制度以及相对较小的国有工业部门不变，同时“让农民老马放开跑”（用列宁的话说），发展农业和手工业。
en: When Deng Xiaoping began his reform in 1979, 80 percent of China’s population was rural. Hence, by merely relaxing the commune system and letting the peasants produce freely, most of the population could experience a great expansion of prosperity, and the economy as a whole could show a surge of growth rates of some 10 to 15 percent annually over a decade. By contrast, in the Soviet Union the devastating consequences of collectivization and the huge agrarian bureaucracy precluded any such rapid economic upturn. Moreover, Stalin had been a “success,” in the sense of creating a mammoth industrial plant and building a superpower; Mao had been a failure as a state-builder with his wild Leap Forward and his inane Cultural Revolution. Gorbachev thus had to liquidate much of what his country regarded as its glory; Deng only had to overcome policies that most in his country wanted to be rid of. Gorbachev therefore had to proceed slowly and indirectly by restructuring his country’s administrative structures through “democratisation”; Deng could leave his political system, together with its relatively small state industrial sector, in place, while “giving the peasant nag its head” (to quote Lenin) in agriculture and artisan production.

zh: 简言之，在毛泽东的斯大林主义失败后，中国可以回到党国与市场结合的新经济政策模式；俄罗斯不能，因为她的斯大林主义成功摧毁了作为该公式前提的农民公民社会。因此，戈尔巴乔夫必须先通过政治改革软化斯大林主义制度，市场化才能走得很远。而当事情陷入僵局——如代表大会之后那样——如果改革要保持可信，他就不能诉诸镇压。但当中国的经济自由化产生其政治对应物时，邓小平的改革使镇压完全可行，因为镇压不会在经济发展方面带来过多成本。
en: In short, after the failed Stalinism of Mao, China could return to the NEP formula of the Party-state plus the market; Russia could not, because her Stalinism had successfully destroyed the peasant civil society that was the precondition for that formula. Gorbachev therefore first had to soften up the Stalinist system by political reform before marketization could proceed very far. And when matters reached an impasse, as they did in the wake of the Congress, he could not resort to repression if

were to remain credible. But when economic liberalization in China produced its political counterpart, Deng’s reform made repression all too feasible, for repression would not entail an undue cost in terms of economic development.

zh: 最薄弱的环节断裂：1989年
en: THE WEAKEST LINK SNAPS: 1989

zh: 如果中国是改革命运的警示案例，那么东欧决定了整个冒险的结局。人民民主国家，这个斯大林主义帝国曾经的骄傲，一直是共产主义链条中最薄弱的一环——借用列宁对俄罗斯在资本主义中位置的描述。然而在1989年，它们成为整个苏联制度的致命危机点。第一次，“社会主义的成果”被证明是“可逆的”，而且是大规模可逆；如果它们能在如此广大的地区被逆转，就没有理由认为它们在别处不能被逆转。
en: If China served as a cautionary example for the fortunes of

, Eastern Europe determined the outcome of the whole adventure. The People’s Democracies, the sometime pride of the Stalinist empire, had always been the weakest link in the Communist chain—to paraphrase Lenin’s characterization of Russia’s place in capitalism. In 1989, however, they became the point of fatal crisis for the entire Soviet system. For the first time the “conquests of socialism” proved to be “reversible,” and on a massive scale; and if they could be reversed in so huge an area, there was no reason why they could not be reversed anywhere.

zh: 从6月波兰选举，经11月柏林墙倒塌，到12月齐奥塞斯库垮台，这一连串事件是共产主义解体中最令人震惊的插曲。四十年积累的压抑与不满爆发，六个政权在七个月内崩溃，每一场危机都比前一场成熟得更快。正如蒂莫西·加顿·阿什总结这个
：在波兰花了十年，在匈牙利花了十个月，在东德花了十周，在捷克斯洛伐克花了十天。
en: The chain reaction of events leading from the Polish elections of June, through the collapse of the Berlin Wall in November, to the fall of Ceausescu in December is the most stunning episode in the disintegration of Communism. Releasing the pent-up frustrations of forty years, six regimes collapsed in the space of seven months, and each crisis matured more rapidly than its predecessor. As Timothy Garton Ash summed up this
: what in Poland had taken ten years, in Hungary took ten months, in East Germany ten weeks, and in Czechoslovakia ten days.

zh: 在一个层面上，这场大内爆很容易解释：东欧政权生于征服，从未具有合法性；因此，一有机会，它们的人民就把它们抛弃，每个民族都因前一个的成功而壮胆。但在另一个层面上，还有许多问题需要解释，因为一切都取决于获得这一机会，而这又取决于莫斯科的意图和勃列日涅夫主义的地位。而在改革的四年里，局势过于含糊，东欧人不敢冒险采取任何大胆行动。
en: On one level this grand implosion is very simple to explain: the East European regimes, born of conquest, had never been legitimate; hence, at the first opportunity their populations threw them off, each nation emboldened by the success of a predecessor. But on another level there is quite a bit to explain, for everything depended on getting that first opportunity, which in turn depended on the intentions of Moscow and the status of the Brezhnev Doctrine. And for four years of
the situation was too ambiguous for the East Europeans to risk any bold action.

zh: 一切结束之后，西方不时听到戈尔巴乔夫“解放”了东欧的说法；的确，他早在1990年就这样说，退休后说得更强烈。但既然政治领袖通常不会把别国从自己政府的控制下解放出来，这种看法需要限定。戈尔巴乔夫及其助手确实设想对东欧进行重大改组，那必将会使该地区自由化，但这绝不意味着他们打算牺牲第二次世界大战的成果或解散华沙条约。相反，他们最初的设想因应对事件压力的即兴发挥而膨胀，直到他们突然失去对局势的控制。由此产生的无意革命，与苏联国内那场最初但进展较慢的对应革命如出一辙。
en: After it was all over it was not infrequently heard in the West that Gorbachev had “liberated” Eastern Europe; indeed, he himself was saying this as early as 1990, and he put it even more strongly after his retirement. But since a political leader does not normally liberate countries from his own government, this view requires qualification. Gorbachev and his aides did in fact have in mind a policy of major restructuring for Eastern Europe that would have certainly liberalized the area, but this by no means signifies that they intended to sacrifice the gains of the Second World War or to dissolve the Warsaw Pact. Rather, their original design was inflated through improvisations in response to the pressure of events to the point where they suddenly lost control of the situation. And the resulting inadvertent revolution was of a piece with its original but slower-moving counterpart in the Soviet Union itself.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫最初对东欧的设想，是苏联关于各条通往社会主义道路的标准学说的更新版。

这意味着应积极鼓励兄弟国家在享有相当自主权的同时，大致沿苏联改革的方向开展各自的改革。到1987—1988年，这一设想在戈尔巴乔夫和雅科夫列夫意识形态的影响下扩展，那是一种建立在“全人类价值”和把苏联世界整合进“共同欧洲家园”基础上的现代化社会主义。在这种新视角中，人民民主国家将在俄罗斯与西方之间、社会主义与资本主义之间扮演桥梁角色，作为一种现代发展的第三条道路。这一愿景并不意味着社会主义作为最高价值被取代；相反，意图是在当代条件下发挥社会主义的潜力。此外，整个纲领——如果可以这样称呼的话——并未经过仔细思考，戈尔巴乔夫政策的推动力很大程度上在于实际政治关切。
en: Gorbachev’s original design for Eastern Europe was an updated version of the standard Soviet doctrine of separate paths to socialism.
This meant that the fraternal countries should be actively encouraged to “make their

” roughly along the lines of the Soviet effort, though with a large degree of autonomy. By 1987-1988 this design had been expanded under the influence of Gorbachev’s and Yakovlev’s ideology of a modernized socialism founded on “universal human values” and integration of the Soviet world into a “common European home.” In this new perspective the People’s Democracies were to play a bridging role between Russia and the West, between socialism and capitalism, as a kind of third way of modern development. This vision did not mean that socialism was superseded as the supreme value; the intention, rather, was to bring out socialism’s potential under contemporary conditions. Besides, the whole program, if it can be called that, had not been carefully thought out, and the spur to Gorbachev’s policy lay largely in practical political concerns.

zh: 这些关切与兄弟党实际遵循的不同道路有关。虽然每个社会主义国家都有权走自己的单独道路，但从莫斯科的角度看，有些道路显然比另一些好。在戈尔巴乔夫看来，雅鲁泽尔斯基的波兰和卡达尔的匈牙利基本上在改革共产主义的正确轨道上。雅鲁泽尔斯基使莫斯科免于干预的代价和负担，而且一旦他镇压了团结工会，从1984年起便推行政治温和政策，释放政治犯，避免与教会发生不必要冲突，并试图使经济自由化。卡达尔掌权三十年后虽已疲惫不堪，却创造了最自由化的社会主义经济，实际上为改革提供了部分样板。然而，其他人民民主国家——东德、捷克斯洛伐克、罗马尼亚和保加利亚——在戈尔巴乔夫看来是四个斯大林—勃列日涅夫式政权组成的“四人帮”，比他自己的政权更需要改组。
en: These concerns related to the different paths the fraternal parties were in fact following. Although every socialist country had the right to its own separate path, from Moscow’s point of view some paths were clearly better than others. From Gorbachev’s perspective, Jaruzelski’s Poland and Kadar’s Hungary were basically on the right track of Reform Communism. Jaruzelski had spared Moscow the cost and the onus of intervention, and once he had suppressed Solidarity, beginning in 1984 he pursued a policy of political moderation, releasing his political prisoners, avoiding unnecessary conflict with the Church, and attempting to liberalize the economy. Kadar, although tired out as an individual after thirty years in power, had nonetheless created the most liberalized socialist economy, which indeed had served as a partial model for

. However, the other People’s Democracies—East Germany, Czechoslovakia, Romania, and Bulgaria—appeared to Gorbachev as a “gang of four” Stalinist-Brezhnevite regimes even more in need of restructuring than his own.

zh: 此外，东欧政治的双重性与苏联的政治分歧重叠，苏联自由派支持匈牙利和波兰，保守派支持另外四国。东德和捷克斯洛伐克是社会主义阵营经济成就的典型（东德甚至在西方也被奇迹般地视为世界级经济成功）；因此苏联保守派用它们来论证改革不必要，国家可以通过完善其传统集中管理模式来克服危机。结果，戈尔巴乔夫不得不越来越急迫地推动这四个顽固抵制改革的国家放弃该模式并“改组”自身。正是通过使四人帮失去信誉、并允许波兰和匈牙利进行越来越大胆的实验来回应国内批评者的需要，在很大程度上解释了他东欧政策的鲁莽。
en: The duality of East European politics, moreover, overlapped with the political division in the Soviet Union, where the liberals favored Hungary and Poland while the conservatives favored the other four. East Germany and Czechoslovakia were the great economic success stories of the socialist camp (East Germany, wondrously, was counted a world-class economic success even in the West); they were therefore used by Soviet conservatives to argue that

was unnecessary and that the country could overcome its crisis by perfecting its traditional centralized model of management. As a consequence, Gorbachev had to push the recalcitrant four ever more urgently to abandon that model and to “restructure” themselves. It was the need to answer his domestic critics by discrediting the gang of four, and by permitting ever bolder experimentation in Poland and Hungary, that explains in large part the rashness of his East European policy.

zh: 此外，莫斯科两个竞争集团在兄弟党内都有盟友，戈尔巴乔夫积极寻求用自己更年轻的人取代东欧旧卫队。旧卫队则把戈尔巴乔夫视为不会持久的冒险家，因此抵制他的改革；昂纳克和胡萨克甚至在自己的地盘禁止苏联改革派出版物。与此同时，东欧党内的改革派分子，以及想要彻底结束制度的异见者，都支持改革和“戈尔比”，有些出于真正信念，但大多数是机会主义。每个人都等着看，在危机中戈尔巴乔夫是否“来真的”，还是会恢复莫斯科过去的做派。
en: Furthermore, both contending groups in Moscow had their allies in the fraternal Parties, and Gorbachev actively sought to replace the East European old guard with his own, younger men. The old guard, for its part, considered Gorbachev an adventurer who would not last, and they therefore stonewalled his

; Honecker and Husak even forbade Soviet reformist publications in their bailiwicks. At the same time, reformist elements within the East European Parties, as well as dissidents who wanted to be done with the system entirely, took up the cause of
and “Gorby,” some out of real conviction, but most opportunistically. And everyone waited to see whether, in a crisis, Gorbachev was “for real” or whether he would revert to previous Muscovite form.

zh: 很可能，直到1989年，戈尔巴乔夫相信不会发生危机，东欧的变化将像国内应该发生的那样按计划、审慎地出现，不需要作出艰难选择。然而实际上，当他在外交政策中开始“新思维”和“全人类价值”时，他就放弃了强制选项。苏联制度复兴所需的西方同情，排除了任何诉诸勃列日涅夫主义的可能。正如波兰的亚当·米赫尼克1988年所说：“戈尔巴乔夫是他外交政策成功的囚徒。”
然而，尽管苏联次要官员如院士奥列格·博戈莫洛夫和外交部发言人根纳季·格拉西莫夫发出了诱人的暗示，说勃列日涅夫主义已死，其消亡从未被明确宣布。因此，1987—1988年之后，东欧危机在发展，各种反对派一边前进一边试探水温。
en: In all probability, until 1989 Gorbachev believed that there would be no crisis, that change in Eastern Europe would occur in “calibrated” fashion just as it was supposed to at home, and that no hard choices would be necessary. In reality, however, he had forfeited the option of coercion when he embarked on his “new thinking” and “universal human values” in foreign policy. The sympathy of the West, necessary for the revival of the Soviet system, precluded any recourse to the Brezhnev Doctrine. As Poland’s Adam Michnik put the matter in 1988, “Gorbachev is the prisoner of his foreign policy successes.”

Yet despite tantalizing hints from such secondary Soviet officials as academician Oleg Bogomolov and Foreign Ministry spokesman Gennadii Gerasimov that the Brezhnev Doctrine was defunct, its demise was never made explicit. Thus, the East European crisis developed after 1987-1988 with the various oppositions testing the waters as they proceeded.

zh: 从1986年开始，戈尔巴乔夫访问了几乎所有东欧首都，敦促变革。1987年，胡萨克被米洛什·雅克什取代为第一书记，但捷克斯洛伐克局势依然如故。1988年5月，卡达尔终于被并不更具冒险精神的卡罗利·格罗斯取代，但这一变化最终导致匈牙利局势解冻。因为格罗斯很快受到伊姆雷·波日高伊领导的激进改革派集团的挑战，而莫斯科以非同寻常的漫不经心，允许匈牙利改革激进化。次年1月至6月间，匈牙利党作出一个又一个史无前例的让步：集会权和结社权得到承认，党的领导作用被放弃，党改名为“社会党”，奥地利边境的铁丝网“墙”被拆除，1956年革命的领导人获得平反，格罗斯被一个由激进改革派主导的四人主席团包围。所有这一切都是在使党现代化、为人民所接受的期望中进行的。这也是在莫斯科批准下、或至少未引起任何反对的情况下进行的，无疑是因为它看起来像是对建设“共同欧洲家园”的贡献。而到1989年夏天，这种改组似乎取得了成功——一个先进改革的绝佳范例。
en: Beginning in 1986, Gorbachev visited virtually all of the East European capitals to urge change. In 1987 Husak was replaced as First Secretary by Milos Jakes, but the situation in Czechoslovakia remained unchanged. In May 1988 Kadar was at last replaced by the hardly more adventurous Karoly Grosz, but this change did eventually lead to the unfreezing of the Hungarian situation. For Grosz was soon challenged by a radical reformist group under the leadership of Imre Pozsgay, and Moscow, with extraordinary insouciance, permitted the Hungarian reform to radicalize. Between January and June of the next year, the Hungarian Party made one unprecedented concession after another: The rights of assembly and of association were granted, the Party’s leading role was abandoned and the Party changed its name to “Socialist,” the barbed wire “wall” at the Austrian frontier was dismantled, the leaders of the 1956 revolution were rehabilitated, and Grosz was hemmed in by a four-man Presidium dominated by radical reformers. All this was undertaken in the expectation of making the Party modern and acceptable to the people. It was also done with Moscow’s approval, or at least without calling forth any objections, no doubt because it seemed to be a contribution to the building of a “common European home.” And as of the summer of 1989, this restructuring appeared to be a success—a fine example of advanced

〔译注〕匈牙利社会主义工人党于1989年10月改组为匈牙利社会党；本段把多个事件放在上半年叙述，时间并不完全相同。

zh: 但东欧最重要的变化发生在波兰，因为那里变革的刺激不是来自党内，而是来自社会。1988年持续的经济衰退引发了1980—1981年以来第一次罢工。虽然团结工会仍属非法，其成员深度参与了这些行动。政权意识到没有团结工会的合作就无法应付经济危机，工会领导层抓住这一情况，迫使党达成分享权力的交易。瓦文萨以自己的声望作担保，说服工人结束罢工，以换取与政权就“反危机公约”进行“圆桌”谈判，尽管团结工会激进派认为这种做法是出卖工会而拒绝。与此同时，党内文官指责执政的将军们背叛制度，雅鲁泽尔斯基及其最亲密同事不得不威胁辞职，才使中央委员会回心转意。1989年初，圆桌会议在教会参与支持下召开，达成了一项交易。
en: But the most important change in Eastern Europe occurred in Poland, for there the stimulus for transformation came not from within the Party but from society. In 1988 continuing economic decline provoked the first strikes since 1980-1981. Although Solidarity was still illegal, its members were deeply involved in these actions. The regime realized it could not cope with the economic crisis without Solidarity’s cooperation, and the union’s leadership seized on this circumstance to pressure the Party into a deal for power sharing. Walesa put his prestige on the line by persuading the workers to end their strike in return for “round-table” negotiations with the regime for an “anticrisis pact,” even though the radical wing of Solidarity rejected this approach as a sellout of the union. At the same time, the civilian Party accused the ruling generals of betraying the system, and Jaruzelski and his closest colleagues had to threaten to resign in order to bring the Central Committee around. At the beginning of 1989 the round table met under the sponsorship of the Church, and a deal was struck.

zh: 团结工会合法化，选举定于6月举行。议会（Sejm）三分之二席位保留给党及其两个长期卫星党——农民党和民主党；团结工会获准为三分之一席位提出候选人。另设一个100席的参议院，团结工会获准竞争全部席位。雅鲁泽尔斯基将由议会选举为总统。更自由、民主的选举将在四年后举行。因此，党被保证在此之前控制政府，在此期间，团结工会将被期望让工人保持安静，并分担克服经济危机不可避免的痛苦的责任。就团结工会而言，它获得了被承认的反对派地位，以及用四年时间训练自己全面接管权力的可能性。
en: Solidarity was legalized and elections were scheduled for June. Two thirds of the seats in the Sejm were reserved for the Party and its two longtime satellites, the Peasant Party and the Democrats; Solidarity was permitted to put up candidates for one third of the seats. A Senate of a hundred seats was created, and Solidarity was allowed to contest all of them. Jaruzelski was to be elected president by the Sejm. Freer, democratic elections were to take place in four years. Thus the Party was guaranteed control of the government until then, and in the interval Solidarity would be expected to keep the workers quiet and to share responsibility for the inevitable pain of overcoming the economic crisis. Solidarity, for its part, acquired the status of a recognized opposition and the possibility of training to assume full power in four years.

zh: 但一切都未按计划发展。政权以为凭借严密的组织和媒体控制会轻松赢得选举，而团结工会刚从地下走出，组织薄弱，只有一份为此创办的报纸《选举报》（Gazeta Wyborcza）。然而，6月4日结果揭晓时，党显然已失去国家的权力。团结工会赢得100个参议院席位中的99个，以及获准参加的议会选举中的大多数。更重要的是，党未能赢得其保留席位的一半，因为选民划掉了其候选人的名字，使他们失去必要的多数；它只在决选中获得配额，而团结工会在决选中动员起来帮它过关。虽然只有60%的选民投票，但大多数弃权是因为团结工会激进派拒绝参与它认为的共产主义闹剧。
en: But nothing worked out as planned. The regime thought it would win the elections easily because of its tight organization and control of the media, whereas Solidarity, just emerging from the underground, was organizationally weak and had only one newspaper,

, founded for the occasion. When the returns came in on June 4, however, the Party had clearly lost power in the country. Solidarity won 99 of the 100 Senate seats and most of the contests it had been allowed to enter for the Sejm. Even more important, the Party failed to win half of its reserved seats because voters crossed off its candidates’ names, thus depriving them of the necessary majority; it received its quota only in runoffs, where Solidarity mobilized to help it along. Although only 60 percent of the electorate voted, most of the abstentions were due to the refusal of the radical wing of Solidarity to take part in what it considered a Communist farce.

〔译注〕团结工会在6月4日和18日两轮投票后共获99个参议院席位；作者把两轮的最终结果压缩在一起叙述。

zh: 这场选举逆转的结果是，双方都陷入困境。政权失去了合法性的一切表象，但团结工会无法接管权力，因为它尚未准备好执政，而且预期莫斯科会抵制。因此，双方起初都假装遵守圆桌协议。雅鲁泽尔斯基当选总统，但只以一票之差，而且是故意计错票。尽管如此，议会仍无法让自己认可一位共产党总理，僵局随之而来。两个月后，瓦文萨成功地把民主党和农民党从党那里撬开，因为两党成员害怕失去职位和特权。有了这一联盟，团结工会现在拥有议会多数，并提议在“你们的[共产党]总统，我们的[团结工会]总理”的基础上解决危机。
en: As a result of this upset, both sides were in a quandary. The regime had lost all semblance of legitimacy, yet Solidarity could not take power because it was unprepared to govern and because of Moscow’s expected resistance. So both sides at first pretended to observe the round-table agreement. Jaruzelski was elected president, but by only one vote, and that on a deliberate miscount. Still, the Sejm could not bring itself to endorse a Communist prime minister, and stalemate ensured. After two months, Walesa succeeded in prying the! Democrats and the Peasants from the Party because their members were fearful of losing their positions and perquisites. With this alliance, Solidarity now had a parliamentary majority, and it proposed to resolve the crisis on the basis of “your [Communist] president, our [Solidarity] prime minister.”

zh: 但这将是一场重大变化，因此必须征求莫斯科的意见。8月底，戈尔巴乔夫打电话给波兰新的文职党首，敦促接受联合政府，或至少表示莫斯科不会反对。至此终于明确，勃列日涅夫主义（几乎）死了。9月，首个后共产主义政府在天主教社会派人士塔德乌什·马佐维耶茨基领导下上台，尽管共产党少数派仍控制着国防和内政等关键部。鉴于波兰案例的历史特殊性，莫斯科很可能认为这是保护苏联在该战略地区利益的最佳方式，因此即使与非共产党人组成联合政府，也是改革的一种可接受变体。
en: But this would be a momentous change, and consequently Moscow had to be consulted. In late August Gorbachev telephoned Poland’s new civilian Party chief and urged acceptance of the coalition, or at least indicated that Moscow would do nothing to oppose it. At last it had been made clear that the Brezhnev Doctrine was (almost) dead. In September the first-ever post-Communist government anywhere came to power under the Social Catholic Tadeusz Mazowiecki, though a Communist minority still controlled the key ministries of defense and interior. Given the historical particularities of the Polish case, Moscow probably reasoned that this was the best way to safeguard Soviet interests in that strategic area, and that even a coalition with non-Communists was therefore an acceptable variant of

zh: 但当然，制度的解体并没有随着这一妥协而停止，正如它没有随着圆桌协议而停止一样。在政治上，波兰人在接下来一年半里相当谨慎：他们清除了秘密警察、共产党部长、官名录机关，最终还清除了雅鲁泽尔斯基本人，但都是一步步进行的。然而在经济上，团结工会领导的政府从一开始就很激进。在新任财政部长莱谢克·巴尔采罗维奇的倡议下，它采取了共产主义世界第一个真正经济转型纲领：通过“休克疗法”向市场和私有财产过渡，与社会主义过去彻底决裂，从而违反了制度的两大禁忌。人们终于从党国解体中得出了经济方面的结论，而这件事肯定没有与莫斯科商量过，那里仍然不能讨论这类想法。1989年秋制定的波兰价格自由化和货币改革纲领，于1990年1月1日作为“大爆炸”启动。连同党国的拆除，这一经济纲领第一次揭示了“退出共产主义”的具体含义，波兰范例成为其他地方这一进程的试点。
en: But of course the system’s unraveling did not stop with this compromise anymore than it had with the round-table agreements. Politically, the Poles were fairly cautious over the next year and a half: They eliminated the secret police, the Communist ministers, the

apparat, and eventually Jaruzelski himself, but only by steps. Yet economically, the Solidarity-led government was radical from the start. On the initiative of the new minister of finance, Leszek Balcerowicz, it adopted the first program of genuine economic transformation in the Communist world: a clean break with the socialist past through a “shock therapy” transition to the market and private property, a violation of the two great taboos of the system. At last the economic conclusions were drawn from the disintegration of the Party-state, and this was something that had surely not been cleared with Moscow, where such ideas could still not be discussed. Elaborated in the fall of 1989, the Polish program of price liberalization and monetary reform was begun as a “big bang” on January 1, 1990. Together with the dismantling of the Party-state, this economic program revealed for the first time what the “exit from Communism” meant concretely, and the Polish example became the pilot for that process elsewhere.

zh: 到1989年秋，这一进程在东欧其余地区全面展开。下一步由匈牙利迈出。9月，布达佩斯开放了与奥地利的边界，这一行动达到了预期的效果：让成千上万东德“度假者”离开本国前往西德。这一行动的公开目的，是向匈牙利民众以及匈牙利需要其援助的西德政府表明，政权确实进行了改革。但由于这一举动明显违反匈牙利与东德的条约，问题就来了：这一举动是否也是莫斯科建议的，作为破坏东德政权——四人帮中最公开反抗者——的一种方式？无论如何，东德人现在开始涌入西德驻布拉格和华沙大使馆，随之而来的外逃使东德陷入公开危机，全国爆发要求改革的大规模示威。
en: By the fall of 1989, that progress was in full swing throughout the rest of Eastern Europe. The next step was taken by Hungary. In September, Budapest opened its frontier with Austria, an action that had the quite intended effect of permitting thousands of East German “vacationers” to leave their country for West Germany. The declared purpose of this action was to demonstrate to the Hungarian population as well as to the West German government, whose aid Hungary needed, that the regime had indeed reformed. But since this move was in clear violation of Hungary’s treaty with East Germany, the question arises whether the move had also been suggested by Moscow as a way of undermining the-East German regime, the most openly defiant of the “gang of four.” In any event, East Germans now began to pour into West German embassies in Prague and Warsaw, and the ensuing exodus threw East Germany into open crisis, with massive demonstrations for reform taking place throughout the country.

zh: 9月7日，不知疲倦的旅行者戈尔巴乔夫抵达柏林，参加东德建国四十周年庆典，在那里受到“戈尔比”和“自由”的呼喊欢迎。他唯一公开批评昂纳克的话是“生活会惩罚那些拖延的人”，但显然一段时间以来，他一直想用一位正在一旁等待的本地改革候选人取代东德第一书记。戈尔巴乔夫终于在下个月如愿。10月16日，昂纳克下令对莱比锡约15万人的示威使用武力，但被其副手埃贡·克伦茨撤销；两天后，克伦茨接任党的最高职位。在这种危险条件下，克伦茨和新总理汉斯·莫德罗在本地人民阵线“新论坛”的支持下尝试改革，该阵线许多成员只想要革新的社会主义，而不是退出共产主义。但这一迟来的努力可怜地失败了，因为10月16日之后已清楚，无论柏林还是莫斯科都不会对民众使用武力，而没有武力，民众就不再服从。于是，当政权在11月9日作为进一步和解姿态开放柏林墙、仅仅允许自由通行时，柏林人的回应是把它拆掉。这一事件标志着政权的终结：改革共产主义政府让位给联合政府，最终举行选举时，党失败了，其国家很快消失。
en: On September 7, Gorbachev, the indefatigable traveller, arrived in Berlin for the fortieth anniversary of the founding of the East German state, where he was greeted with cries of “Gorby” and “Freedom.” His only public criticism of Honecker was the remark “life punishes those who delay,” but it is clear that for some time he had desired to replace the East German First Secretary with one of the local reform candidates waiting in the wings. Gorbachev finally got his wish the following month. On October 16, Honecker’s order to use force against a demonstration of some 150,000 people in Leipzig was countermanded by his deputy, Egon Krenz, who two days later moved into the top Party post. Under these parlous conditions, Krenz and a new prime minister, Hans Modrow, attempted a

with the support of the local popular front, Neues Forum, many of whose members wanted only a reformed socialism, not an exit from Communism. But this belated effort fizzled pitifully, for after October 16 it was clear that neither Berlin nor Moscow would use force against the population, and without force the population would no longer obey. Accordingly, when in a further gesture of conciliation the regime on November 9 opened the Wall simply to allow free passage, the Berliners responded by tearing it down. And that event marked the end of the regime: the Reform Communist government gave way to a coalition, and when elections were finally held, the Party lost and its state soon disappeared.

〔译注〕戈尔巴乔夫为东德建国四十周年访问东柏林是在1989年10月6日至7日，而非9月7日；莱比锡10月9日和16日均有大规模示威。

zh: 东德革命的冲击决定了前集团其余地区共产主义的命运。1989年10月，匈牙利共产党人为他们早先的大胆付出了代价：他们做得过头，放弃列宁主义，转向“民主社会主义”。他们把自己的党改名为“社会党”，并要求所有成员重新登记加入新组织。结果，70万党员中只有3万人选择留在党内，党因此被迫安排它必将在次年输掉的选举。11月，捷克斯洛伐克人终于把事情掌握在自己手中；自8月以来，莫斯科一直徒劳地催促其领导人改变方向。他们目睹东德政权被如此轻易地清算，于是在天鹅绒革命中以更小的力气处理了自己的党国。
en: The shock of the East German revolution sealed the fate of Communism throughout the rest of the erstwhile bloc. In October 1989, the Hungarian Communists were repaid for their earlier daring when they overreached themselves by abandoning Leninism in favor of “democratic socialism.” They renamed their party “Socialist” and called for the reenrollment of all members in the new organization. As a result, only thirty thousand out of seven hundred thousand members chose to remain in the Party, which was thus forced to schedule elections it was sure to lose for the following year. In November the Czechoslovaks, whose leaders had been vainly prodded by Moscow to change direction since August, at last took things into their own hands. Having witnessed the ease with which the East German regime was liquidated, they dispatched their own Party-state with even less effort in the Velvet Revolution.

zh: 于是只剩下巴尔干的强硬政权。在保加利亚，日夫科夫于11月被一场实际上由苏联导演的宫廷革命取代；随后是通常的进程：从改革共产主义政府到联合政府再到选举。在这次事件中，共产党人赢得选举，但稍后失去权力。在罗马尼亚，该地区最坏的政权遭遇了最坏的命运——12月一场真正的暴力革命。罗马尼亚的剧变也是东欧最神秘的。匈牙利电视台传播的邻国事件榜样点燃了罗马尼亚革命，但这场革命很可能被党的忠实分子接管，他们基本上想除掉齐奥塞斯库，以尽可能保住自己的地位。他们也可能受到莫斯科的鼓励，因为众所周知，戈尔巴乔夫极端厌恶齐奥塞斯库及其完全未改革的社会主义。无论如何，随着该地区所有其他共产主义都已消失，最坏的典范几乎不可能希望长期存活。
en: There thus remained only the hard-core regimes of the Balkans. In Bulgaria, Zhivkov was replaced in November by what was in effect a Soviet-directed palace revolution; there then ensued the usual progression from a Reform Communist government to a coalition to elections. In this case the Communists won the elections only to lose power somewhat later. In Romania, the worst regime of the area met the worst fate, an actual violent revolution, in December. Romania’s was also the most mysterious of the East European upheavals. Ignited by the example of events in neighboring countries as conveyed through Hungarian television, the Romanian revolution was in all probability taken over by Party loyalists who basically wanted to remove Ceausescu in order to save what they could of their positions, And it is also possible that they were encouraged to do this by Moscow, for it is well known that Gorbachev had an extreme antipathy for Ceausescu and his totally unreconstructed socialism. In any event, with all the other Communisms in the area gone, the worst exemplar of all could hardly hope to survive for long.

zh: 甚至苏联轨道之外的共产主义也被这场溃败削弱。第一个改革共产主义，即制度最初的异见者南斯拉夫，也开始解体。1980年铁托去世后，他留下的修订制度又相当好地维持了十年。然后在1990年，紧接苏联东欧崩溃之后，南斯拉夫国内局势并未发生任何危机，同样的后共产主义议程却突然变得紧迫：民主、市场化和私有化。但这里的结局远比别处可怕，而民族主义本身只是问题的一部分。这场悲剧的一个重要方面，是垂死的党国及其军队利用塞尔维亚民族主义，以便在可能的地方挽救自己的地位。结果是一种民族布尔什维主义——借用1920年代德国政治的一个术语——与齐奥塞斯库之后的罗马尼亚或某些较落后的前苏联共和国不无相似之处。最后，小国阿尔巴尼亚的政权也崩溃了，原因仅仅是它所依据的模式已经消失。
en: Even Communisms outside the Soviet orbit were undermined by this debacle. The first Reform Communism, that of the original dissident of the system, Yugoslavia, also began to unravel. After Tito’s death in 1980, the revised system he had bequeathed held together reasonably well for another decade. Then in 1990, in the immediate wake of the collapse of Soviet Eastern Europe, suddenly and without any crisis in internal Yugoslav conditions, the same post-Communist agenda as elsewhere became urgent: democracy, marketization, and privatization. But here the outcome was far more dire than elsewhere, and nationalism as such was only part of the problem. A major aspect of the tragedy was the exploitation of Serbian nationalism by the dying Party-state and its army in order to salvage its positions where it could. The result was a kind of national Bolshevism—to use a term from German politics of the 1920s—not without parallels with post-Ceausescu Romania or certain of the more backward ex-Soviet republics. Finally, the regime in little Albania also collapsed, and for no other reason than that the model on which it was based had disappeared.

〔译注〕南斯拉夫在1990年以前已有严重的外债、通货膨胀和政治紧张；作者所谓当时没有国内危机是过于笼统的概括。

zh: 但这场大内爆最耐人寻味的方面，是它与母本模式的关系。莫斯科显然以某种方式推动所有卫星国走向改革，但同样显然，它并不希望出现这样的结果。的确，即使外部帝国已在大规模崩溃，戈尔巴乔夫仍未意识到正在发生什么。直到德国十月革命，他和波日高伊、克伦茨等“小戈尔巴乔夫”仍把正在展开的事态视为改革的前进步伐；甚至齐奥塞斯库的清除也被看作改革共产主义取得的一次胜利。的确，直到1989年深秋，从团结工会到捷克公民论坛的各种反对派仍在担心危险的“红线”在哪里。直到新年之后，双方才开始明白权力平衡已发生巨大转变；但那时莫斯科已经太晚，无法采取任何行动。
en: But the most intriguing aspect of this Grand Implosion is its relationship to the master model. Moscow had clearly prodded all of its satellites in one way or another on the way to reform, but just as clearly it had not desired the result. Indeed, even when the External Empire was well on its way to collapse, Gorbachev failed to realize what was happening. As late as the German October revolution, he, as well as such “little Gorbachevs” as Pozsgay and Krenz, viewed what was unfolding as the forward march of

; even the elimination of Ceausescu was greeted as a blow struck for Reform Communism. Indeed, until well into the autumn of 1989 the various oppositions, from Solidarity to the Czech Civic Forum, were still worrying about where the “red line” of danger might be. It was only after the new year that it began to sink in on both sides of the barricades that an enormous shift in the balance of power had occurred; but by then it was too late for Moscow to do anything about it.

zh: 事实上，在1989年过程中，从来没有任何时候苏联能够对此采取行动。如我们所见，莫斯科已经无法维持高加索的公共秩序。因此，毫不奇怪，在两个关键国家波兰和东德进行所需规模的干预，现已超出苏联的军事和经济资源。尽管莫斯科已有30万军队驻在当地，但他们已被改革弄得士气低落；在国内，应征入伍者拒绝报到，国库空虚。在政治上和心理上，干预更不可行，因为它会疏远当时已不可或缺的西方，破坏国内对改革的支持，并使戈尔巴乔夫受制于决不会手软的军方和保守派。所以戈尔巴乔夫“解放”了东欧，却不知道自己在这样做，也因为他没有别的办法。
en: In fact, during the course of 1989 there was never a time when the Soviet Union could have done anything about it. As we have seen, Moscow was already unable to maintain public order in the Caucasus. It is therefore hardly surprising that intervention on the scale required in the two crucial countries, Poland and East Germany, was now beyond the Soviets’ military and economic resources. Although Moscow had three hundred thousand troops already on the spot, they had been demoralized by

; at home, draftees were refusing to report to duty and the treasury was bare. Politically and psychologically, intervention was even less feasible because it would have alienated the now indispensable West, destroyed support for

at home, and thrown Gorbachev onto the not-too-tender mercies of his military and the conservatives. So Gorbachev “liberated” Eastern Europe not knowing that this was what he was doing, and because he did not have the means to do otherwise.

zh: 他的整个政策建立在一种错误信念上：如果向东欧人提供真正革新的社会主义，他们会热切回应，而且外面有许多小一号的戈尔巴乔夫会这样做。他悲哀地低估了人民对共产主义的厌恶以及外部帝国中民族情绪的力量，正如他低估了内部帝国中的同样力量。但一旦他的算计被证明错误，他就尽可能对由此产生的崩溃作有利于自己的解释。他对失败作了创造性的适应，把崩溃说成解放并揽功，以挽救国内的改革事业并保持西方的尊重。
en: His whole policy had been based on the mistaken belief that the East Europeans would eagerly respond to a genuine reformed socialism if it were offered to them, and that there were many lesser Gorbachevs out there to do just that. He woefully underestimated the people’s loathing of Communism and the power of national sentiment in the External Empire, just as he underestimated these same forces within the Internal Empire. But once his calculations had proved themselves mistaken, he put the best face possible on the resulting collapse. He made a creative adaptation to defeat by taking credit for the collapse as a liberation in order to salvage the cause of
at home and to keep the esteem of the West.

zh: 上层建筑消融：1990年
en: THE SUPERSTRUCTURE DISSOLVES: 1990

zh: 随着1990新年的到来，东欧解放的回力镖越过苏联边界飞回，加剧了一场当时已迅速成熟的内部危机。危机以四种相互关联的形式逼近。第一，争取共和国主权的运动正走向联盟解体；第二，经济改革的尝试正退化为经济崩溃；第三，苏联民主化正变成对党权力的拆除；第四和最后，俄罗斯总统叶利钦开始盖过苏联总统戈尔巴乔夫。
en: With the new year of 1990, the boomerang of Eastern European liberation came back across the Soviet frontier to aggravate a by-now rapidly maturing internal crisis. The crisis was approaching in four interrelated forms. First, the drive for republic sovereignty was moving toward the disintegration of the Union; second, the attempt at economic reform was degenerating into the collapse of the economy; third, Soviet democratization was turning into the dismantling of Party power; and fourth and finally, Russian President Yeltsin was beginning to eclipse Soviet President Gorbachev.

zh: 政权最后两年的行动结构可以概括如下。1990年头九个月，国家在这四种力量的推动下向左转，到初秋，似乎“向民主和市场的过渡”（改革者现在这样说的）已迫在眉睫，戈尔巴乔夫将会接受。然后，在9月，对这种全面变化的不可避免的反动出现了，戈尔巴乔夫换了阵营，保守趋势在整个冬季一直深化到1991年春天。这一反动反过来又激起“民主派”的动员，导致叶利钦于1991年7月由普选当选总统。最后，为了拼命阻止这一来自左翼的新威胁，旧卫队于8月发动政变，名义上针对戈尔巴乔夫，实际上针对叶利钦及其代表的激进变革力量。阴谋者可笑的失败最终证明，制度已失去强制、甚至为生存而战的力量。于是，整个结构干脆崩溃：党在8月，联盟在12月。
en: The structure of action during the last two years of the regime may be summarized as follows. During the first nine months of 1990, the country was driven leftward under the propulsion of these four forces, and by early fall it seemed as if the “transition to democracy and the market” (as reformers were now saying) was imminent and Gorbachev would accept it. Then, in September, the inevitable reaction to such sweeping change emerged, Gorbachev changed sides, and the conservative trend deepened throughout the winter and into the spring of 1991. This reaction, in turn, provoked a mobilization of the “democrats” which led to Yeltsin’s election as president by universal suffrage in July 1991. Finally, in a desperate effort to head off this renewed threat from the left, the old guard in August staged a putsch, nominally against Gorbachev but in fact against Yeltsin and the forces of radical change he represented. The ludicrous failure of the plotters at last demonstrated that the system had lost the strength to coerce, or even to fight for its survival. And so, the whole structure simply collapsed, the Party in August, the Union in December.

〔译注〕叶利钦于1991年6月12日当选俄罗斯总统，7月10日宣誓就职；原书把当选时间写为7月。

zh: 走向这一结局的第一次公开行动发生在1990年初的立陶宛。为了避免在共和国失去所有支持，立陶宛共产党在前一年12月退出了苏联党。这是闻所未闻的行动，因为苏共的单一整体性质既是其权力垄断的保证，也是维系联盟的唯一真正纽带。因此，戈尔巴乔夫决心在波罗的海国家抵抗他刚在东欧让步的事情，并于1月抵达维尔纽斯与立陶宛领导人会谈。约25万人从共和国各地来到首都，示威支持独立。连续三天，戈尔巴乔夫在苏联电视上恳求人群：他声称，与苏联经济保持一体化符合这个小共和国的自身利益。但这种功利主义论证没有打动任何人。
en: The first overt move toward this outcome occurred in Lithuania at the beginning of 1990. In order to avoid losing all support in the republic, the Lithuanian Communist Party had seceded from the Soviet Party the previous December. This was an unheard-of action, for the monolithic nature of the Soviet Party was both the guarantee of its monopoly of power and the only real bond that held the Union together. Accordingly, Gorbachev determined to resist in the Baltic states what he had just conceded in Eastern Europe, and in January he arrived in Vilnius for discussions with the Lithuanian leadership. Some 250,000 people came to the capital from across the republic to demonstrate support for independence. For three days Gorbachev was seen on Soviet television pleading with the crowds: it was in the tiny republic’s self-interest, he claimed, to remain integrated with the Soviet economy. But this utilitarian argument swayed no one.

zh: 立陶宛人继续前进，2月，民族解放运动萨尤迪斯在地方苏维埃选举中大获全胜。新的最高苏维埃即议会随后选举萨尤迪斯领袖维陶塔斯·兰茨贝吉斯为总统，3月11日，议会宣布国家独立。尽管莫斯科威胁性地在维尔纽斯周围展示了一些装甲车，但它不敢像在高加索那样使用武力，而是诉诸经济封锁。此外，由于苏联宪法名义上承认分离权，戈尔巴乔夫让联盟最高苏维埃通过一项法律，规定行使该权利须经过复杂的五年程序，实际上使该权利失效。
en: The Lithuanians pressed on, and in February the national liberation movement, Sajudis, won the local soviet elections hands-down. The new Supreme Soviet, or Sejm, then elected Sajudis’s leader, Vytautas Landsbergis, president, and on March 11 it declared the country independent. Although Moscow threateningly paraded some armored vehicles around Vilnius, it did not dare use force as it had in the Caucasus, but resorted instead to an economic blockade. In addition, since the Soviet constitution nominally recognized the right of secession, Gorbachev had the Union Supreme Soviet vote a law stipulating a complex five-year process for exercising that right, a procedure that in effect nullified it.

zh: 这种法律主义的阻挠如今已是无可救药的过时，1990年1月阿塞拜疆更有力地证明了这一点。成千上万阿塞拜疆人在与伊朗的边界上示威，甚至拆毁边境障碍。由人民阵线领导的反对苏维埃政权的骚乱在巴库爆发。莫斯科派军队恢复秩序，但随后似乎又退后，让局势恶化。进一步的暴力很可能由克格勃组织——也许得到莫斯科最高层官员的共谋——以便为与人民阵线全面摊牌提供借口。
1月15日，巴库在一次至少造成60人死亡的行动中被从阵线手中夺回。这是改革年代第二次流血事件。它也标志着把阿塞拜疆留在联盟内的任何可能性终结。与此同时，摩尔达维亚第一次表现出不满，人群示威要求与罗马尼亚重新合并，这在上个月齐奥塞斯库垮台之前是不可想象的。
en: That such legalistic obstructionism was now a hopeless anachronism was demonstrated even more forcefully in Azerbaijan, again in January 1990. Thousands of Azerbaijani demonstrated on the border with Iran, even tearing up frontier barriers. Riots against Soviet power, led by the Popular Front, broke out in Baku. Moscow brought in troops to restore order, but it then appeared to draw back to let the situation deteriorate. Further violence was probably organized by the KGB—and perhaps with the complicity of officials at the highest levels in Moscow—to provide a pretext for an all-out showdown with the Popular Front.
On January 15, Baku was retaken from the Front in an action that cost at least sixty lives. This was the second bloody incident of the

years. It also marked the end of any possibility of keeping Azerbaijan in the Union. Simultaneously, Moldavia for the first time began to show its disaffection as crowds demonstrated for reunion with Romania, something unthinkable before the fall of Ceaușescu the previous month.

zh: 于是，沿着联盟欧洲部分的所有边界，存在一个新的“苏联人民”的观念被揭穿为幻想。始于1988年2月卡拉巴赫爆炸的进程，以1990年1月立陶宛的脱离和巴库的镇压而完成。戈尔巴乔夫试图把他所说的“强大的中心与强大的共和国”这两种相互竞争的要求调和起来，结果失败了。
en: Thus, all along the frontiers of the European part of the Union, the idea that there existed a new “Soviet people” was exposed as an illusion. The process that had begun with the explosion of Karabakh in February 1988 was completed with the defection of Lithuania and the suppression of Baku in January 1990. Gorbachev’s effort to square the circle of the competing claims of “a strong center and strong republics,” as he put it, had ended in failure.

zh: 这些边疆脱离对中心的直接影响，是在制度顶端引发政治危机。一旦东欧革命不会在边界停下的前景变得明显，戈尔巴乔夫的地位便第一次受到严重威胁。在1月的一次中央委员会全会上，他因最近的灾难遭到如此猛烈的批评风暴，以致地位“悬于一线”。全会进行期间，他被派往维尔纽斯；此前全会向他发出了相当于最后通牒的要求：要么结束叛乱，要么下台，让位给愿意使用更强硬手段的人。看来他之所以幸存，只是因为他以提出辞职冒险，料定全会不会在如此危险的危机中接受。但无论这次仍有些神秘的会议的细节如何，到2月，整个改革进程显然正在被重新思考。
en: The immediate effect of these border defections on the center was to provoke a political crisis at the top of the system. Once it became apparent that the revolution in Eastern Europe would not stop at the frontier, Gorbachev’s position was for the first time seriously threatened. At a Central Committee plenum in January, he was subjected to such a storm of criticism for the recent disasters that his position “hung by a hair.” He was sent to Vilnius while the plenum was underway, after that body had issued to him what amounted to an ultimatum: Either end the sedition or step down in favor of someone willing to use stronger means. It seems that he survived only by offering his resignation on the dare the plenum would not accept it in the midst of so dangerous a crisis. But whatever the details of this still somewhat mysterious meeting, it is clear that by February the whole course of
was being rethought.

zh: 第一个变化是放弃党的领导作用。戈尔巴乔夫在整个1989年坚决拒绝考虑放弃党的领导作用，现在却在2月续开的全会上敦促并不情愿的中央委员会接受。随着人民阵线在联盟内激增，领导作用已经是一个虚构；而东欧各国党已经放弃霸权要求，转而通过联合政府勉强分享权力，苏联的第六条已成为令人尴尬的时代错误。因此，现在应当通过明确放弃过去的命令方法、转向“人道、民主的社会主义”——用戈尔巴乔夫的新口号来说——来进一步使制度现代化。这实际上意味着再抛弃一些意识形态压舱物，以保住党的实际地位；因为放弃领导作用、转向名义上的多党制，仍会让
党拥有压倒性的制度化权力。此外，这种变化符合戈尔巴乔夫让党退出公共事务直接管理、并借此使党自身恢复活力的政策。尽管如此，在改革开始时，戈尔巴乔夫从未设想过像当前举措这样大胆的事情；他这样做是在回应不断展开的危机要求而即兴发挥。
en: The first change was the abandonment of the Party’s leading role. What Gorbachev had adamantly refused to contemplate all through 1989 he now urged on a reluctant Central Committee at a continued plenum in February. With Popular Fronts proliferating within the Union, the leading role was already a fiction; and with the Parties of Eastern Europe having already abandoned their claims to hegemony in favor of a tenuous participation in power through coalitions, the Soviets’ Article 6 had become an embarrassing anachronism. It was thus time to modernize the system further by explicitly abandoning the command methods of the past in favor of a “humane, democratic socialism,” as Gorbachev’s new slogan put it. This in effect meant jettisoning yet more ideological ballast in order to preserve the Party’s practical positions; for abandoning the leading role in favor of a nominal multiparty system would still leave

Party with an overwhelming preponderance of institutionalized power. Moreover, such a change was in line with Gorbachev’s policy of removing the Party from the direct management of public affairs and, by so doing, revitalizing the Party itself. Still, at the start of
Gorbachev had never contemplated anything so bold as his current move, and in making it he was improvising in response to the unfolding imperatives of crisis.

zh: 2月底至3月，这些要求继续累积。在期待已久的地方和地区苏维埃选举中，自由派——现在自称“民主派”——取得了自前一年人民代表大会以来一直争取的权力分享突破。年初，跨地区集团、人民阵线和各种“非正式”团体联合组成“民主俄罗斯”。作为一个广泛的“运动”而非政党，民主俄罗斯首先寻求组织整个反对派的地方竞选，然后以新苏维埃为基地，逐步把权力从党转移到社会。简言之，其目标是拆除“极权主义”——民主派现在公开这样称呼这个制度。萨尤迪斯和其他民族人民阵线也在这样做，并同时争取独立。
en: In late February-March these imperatives continued to accumulate. In the long-awaited elections to local and regional soviets, the liberals, now calling themselves “democrats,” made the breakthrough to power sharing that they had been working toward since the Congress of People’s Deputies the previous year. At the beginning of the year the Inter-Regional Group, the Popular Fronts, and various “informals” had coalesced to form Democratic Russia. As a broad “movement,” not a political party, Democratic Russia sought first to organize the local election campaigns of the entire opposition and then, using the new soviets as a base, to gradually transfer power from the Party to society. In short, its goal was to dismantle “totalitarianism,” as the democrats now openly called the system. And Sajudis and the other national Popular Fronts were also out do this, and to achieve independence as well.

zh: 然而，即使在公开性时代，这些目标也不能在电视上播出，也不能出现在仍属党所有、仍受审查的大多数报刊上。尽管如此，人人都知道这些实际上就是选举的赌注，党和民主派都相应紧张。镇压的谣言盛行，因此“民主派”动员起来，在俄罗斯共和国举行第一次街头示威。2月4日，约30万人游行到克里姆林宫，向即将辩论第六条的中央委员会会议施压。阿法纳西耶夫向示威者讲话，呼吁一场新的“二月革命”，他指的是从十月革命的列宁主义原则和平回归二月革命的宪政原则。人群中更大胆的成员举着标语，让党务官僚“记住罗马尼亚”。紧张局势继续升级。自由派呼吁2月25日再次举行大规模示威，一些领导人提出迫使政权进入波兰式“圆桌”谈判以转移权力的目标。此时戈尔巴乔夫本人也感到受威胁，因为新示威也将针对他自己加强总统权力的计划。当局因此试图用电视警告“挑衅”来吓唬民众，第二次游行的队伍确实比第一次小。
en: Yet even in the era of

such aims could not be broadcast on television or appear in most of the press, which was still owned by the Party and still subject to censorship. Nonetheless, everyone knew that these were in fact the stakes in the elections, and both the Party and the democrats were correspondingly tense. Rumors of a crackdown were rife, so the “democrats” mobilized for the first street demonstrations in the Russian republic. On February 4, approximately three hundred thousand people marched to the Kremlin to pressure the Central Committee meeting that was to debate Article 6. Addressing the demonstrators, Afanasiev called for a new “February Revolution,” by which he meant a pacific return from the Leninist principles of October to the constitutionalist principles of February. Bolder members of the crowd carried placards summoning the apparatchiki to “remember Romania.” So tension continued to mount. The liberals called for another mass demonstration on February 25, with some of their leaders advancing the aim of compelling the regime to enter into Polish-style “round-table” negotiations for a transfer of power. By now Gorbachev himself felt threatened because the new demonstration would also be directed against his own plans for a stronger presidency. The authorities therefore attempted to frighten the population with televised warnings of “provocations,” and the crowds on the second march were in fact smaller than those on the first.

zh: 然而几天后，在地方选举中，民主派在莫斯科、列宁格勒、斯维尔德洛夫斯克和俄罗斯联邦其他大城市赢得明显多数。党机关在这些中心的政治控制被打破（尽管它在各省仍基本保持完整）。波罗的海人民阵线，特别是萨尤迪斯，取得了更大的胜利，其选举成功成为立陶宛宣布独立的基础。高加索的民族主义者取得了类似胜利，鲁赫在乌克兰表现良好，尽管党在那里赢得了多数选票。
en: Yet a few days later, in the local elections, the democrats won clear majorities in Moscow, Leningrad, Sverdlovsk, and the other larger cities of the Russian Federation. The political hold of the Party apparat was broken in all of these centers (though it survived substantially intact throughout the provinces). An even greater victory was scored by the Baltic Popular Fronts, and particularly by Sajudis, and its electoral success became the basis for Lithuania’s declaration of independence. The nationalists of the Caucasus achieved comparable victories, and Rukh did well in Ukraine, although there the Party won a majority of the vote.

zh: 在1989年的联盟级选举中，自由派反对派获得了公共讲坛和一个由少数派组成的议会党团。在1990年的地方选举中，这一反对派获得了政治行动的机构基础。总共，联盟约三分之一现在落入那些已超越戈尔巴乔夫改组旧制度政策、转向拆除旧制度以建立新制度的人手中。波波夫成为莫斯科市长，阿纳托利·索布恰克成为列宁格勒市长。叶利钦再次取得胜利，他在斯维尔德洛夫斯克当选俄罗斯最高苏维埃代表时赢得80%多数。在民主派掌权的一切地方，他们开始与机关就行政人员、市政和党财产、税收、报刊和电视的控制权进行拉锯战。
en: In the Union-level elections of 1989, the liberal opposition had gained a public platform and a minority parliamentary caucus. In the local elections of 1990, this opposition gained an institutional base for political action. Altogether, about a third of the Union now passed into the hands of people who had gone beyond Gorbachev’s policy of restructuring the old system to a policy of dismantling it in favor of a new one. Popov became mayor of Moscow and Anatolii Sobchak of Leningrad. Yeltsin scored another triumph when he won an 80 percent majority in his election as a deputy to the Russian Supreme Soviet from Sverdlovsk. And everywhere that the democrats were in power they began a tug-of-war with the apparat over control of administrative staffs, municipal and Party property, tax revenues, the press, and television.

〔译注〕波波夫和索布恰克1990年分别担任莫斯科、列宁格勒市苏维埃主席，1991年才当选各自城市的市长。

zh: 这些变化也意味着上层政策的改变。3月中旬，人民代表大会实施了戈尔巴乔夫使政党合法化的新政策，同时设立了行政总统职位。行政总统被设计得比现有的代表大会主席职位更有权力，将赋予戈尔巴乔夫一种推定的民主合法性，以制衡苏维埃中新近强大的反对力量。它还会给他更高的国际威望，使他成为乔治·布什和弗朗索瓦·密特朗等行政首脑的准平等者。此外，它将给他一个独立于始终敌对的中央委员会的更强权力基础。最后，它将保护他免受下一次党代表大会的影响——其预定日期现已提前到6月底——以防再次出现像1月那样把他赶下党职的企图，或像推翻赫鲁晓夫那样的政变。
en: These changes also meant a change of policy at the top. In mid-March the Congress of People’s Deputies implemented Gorbachev’s new policy of legalizing political parties and at the same time created the post of executive president. Designed to be more powerful than the existing post of chairman of the Congress, the executive presidency would confer on Gorbachev a putative democratic legitimacy as a counterweight to the newly powerful opposition forces in the soviets. It would also give him increased international prestige as the would-be equal of such executives as George Bush and François Mitterrand. In addition, it would give him a stronger power base independent of the ever hostile Central Committee. Finally, it would shield him from the next Party Congress—whose scheduled date had now been moved up to late June—just in case there were another attempt to remove him from Party office like that of January, or like the coup that felled Khrushchev.

〔译注〕戈尔巴乔夫当时担任的是最高苏维埃主席；人民代表大会与最高苏维埃为不同机构。

zh: 唯一的问题是如何组织总统选举。自由派倾向于人民直接投票，许多评论家后来会说，戈尔巴乔夫不走这条路是个错误：他当时仍然受欢迎，一次直接但无竞争的选举会大大增强他的合法性。但这绝非确定：1989年选举中的选民倾向于对无人竞争的党人投“反对”票，如果选民在总统选举中表现出同样倾向，可能导致尴尬的险胜，甚至更糟。到1990年，直接无竞争选举显然是戈尔巴乔夫不能冒的风险，尽管民意调查显示84%的公众倾向于直接选举。于是戈尔巴乔夫的支持者提出反论：危机太严重，不能拖延给国家一个行政首脑。虽然戈尔巴乔夫采取了由苏联代表大会无竞争选举的安全路线，但他仅以49票的优势获得必要的三分之二多数。公平地说，这一脆弱的新尊荣在国外比在国内更受认真对待。
en: The only problem was how to organize the presidential election. The liberals preferred a direct vote by the people, and many commentators would later argue that it was a mistake for Gorbachev not to take that route: he was then still popular, and a direct though unopposed election would have given him a greatly enhanced legitimacy. But this was by no means certain: voters in the 1989 elections had been inclined to vote “no” against unopposed Party figures, and had voters shown the same tendency in a presidential election, it could have led to an embarrassingly close call, or possibly even worse. By 1990 direct unopposed election was clearly a risk Gorbachev could not take, even though polls indicated that direct election was preferred by 84 percent of the public. So Gorbachev’s supporters advanced the counterargument that the crisis was too grave to delay giving the country an executive. Although Gorbachev took the safe route of unopposed election by the Soviet Congress, he gained the necessary two-thirds majority by only forty-nine votes. It is fair to say that this tenuous new dignity was taken more seriously abroad than at home.

zh: 因为新近获得权力的民主派立即提出了新挑战。5月1日，波波夫市长批准一场自发示威作为红场游行的一部分，戈尔巴乔夫在列宁墓上的检阅台上被嘘下台。更严重的是，叶利钦效仿其对手的做法，宣布竞选俄罗斯联邦新最高苏维埃主席团“主席”，该职位实际上将使他成为共和国总统。戈尔巴乔夫正确察觉到威胁，把自己的声望押上，在俄罗斯议会面前反对叶利钦。该机构于2月与市苏维埃同时选举产生，明显比大城市的新政府更保守；其中只有少数民主派，相当一部分是党性的外省人和党务官僚，中间还有一个不小的“沼泽”即摇摆集团。因此，5月底的竞争十分接近：叶利钦只在第三次尝试中获胜，而且仅多四票。
en: For new challenges were immediately forthcoming from the recently empowered democrats. On May 1, Mayor Popov authorized a spontaneous demonstration as a part of the parade through Red Square, and Gorbachev was heckled off the reviewing stand atop Lenin’s Mausoleum. Far more serious, Yeltsin, taking a leaf from his rival’s book, posed his candidacy for “chairman” of the Presidium of the new Supreme Soviet of the Russian Federation, a post that in effect would make him president of the republic. Correctly sensing a threat, Gorbachev put his prestige on the line to oppose Yeltsin before the Russian parliament. That body, elected in February at the same time as the municipal soviets, was distinctly more conservative than the new governments of the big cities; it had only a minority of democrats, a goodly portion of Party-minded provincials and apparatchiki, and a sizeable “marsh,” or swing group, in between. The contest at the end of May was accordingly close: Yeltsin won only on the third try, and by a mere four votes.

〔译注〕叶利钦1990年5月当选俄罗斯最高苏维埃主席，1991年6月才当选俄罗斯总统；波波夫当时是莫斯科市苏维埃主席。

zh: 尽管如此，他还是在戈尔巴乔夫公开反对的情况下赢了，这使他实际上成为与之平起平坐的国家领导人：叶利钦在已经独特的全国最受欢迎政治人物地位之外，又增加了一个重要的机构权力基础。利用这一基础，他效仿立陶宛人的做法，说服议会于6月8日通过俄罗斯主权宣言，作为把权力从中心转移到他和所有其他共和国的手段。飞镖现在完全飞回了家，因为随着俄罗斯处于半分离状态，整个联盟受到致命削弱；在随后几周，所有其他共和国都通过了类似宣言，惊恐的党务官僚称之为“主权游行”。他们确实有理由惊恐，因为主权运动立即引发一场“法律战”，所有共和国都主张有权用自己的立法废止苏联法规。奖品与春天开始的苏维埃与机关之间地方斗争中的一样：对财产、矿权、税收和行政管辖权的控制。到夏末，所有旧结构都在溶解，民主派对抗党务官僚，中心对抗各共和国，争夺废墟的所有权。
en: Still, he had won despite Gorbachev’s open opposition, and this made him virtually a coequal national leader: Yeltsin had added a major institutional power base to his already unique status as the country’s most popular political figure. And using this base, he took a leaf from the Lithuanians’ book and persuaded the parliament on June 8 to vote a Russian declaration of sovereignty as a means for transferring power from the center to his and all the other republics. The boomerang had now come all the way home, for with Russia in a state of semisecession, the Union as a whole was fatally undermined; and in the ensuing weeks all the other republics voted similar declarations in what horrified apparatchiki called a “parade of sovereignties.” And well might they have been horrified, for the sovereignty movement immediately generated a “war of laws” as all the republics asserted the right to nullify Soviet statutes with their own legislation. The prize was the same as in the local battles begun in the spring between the soviets and the apparat: control of property, mineral rights, tax revenues, and administrative jurisdictions. By the end of the summer all the old structures were dissolving, with the democrats pitted against the apparatchiki, and the center against the republics for possession of the rubble.
