〔译注〕俄罗斯国家主权宣言于1990年6月12日通过，而非6月8日；宣言主张共和国法律优先和扩大自治，并非当日正式退出苏联。

zh: 在这一进程——路易十五会称之为“洪水”——之中，戈尔巴乔夫在7月初的第二十八次党代表大会上取得了他最后一次政治胜利。代表大会的目的是戈尔巴乔夫自掌权以来一直追求的那种难以捉摸的机关改革；既然党已失去领导作用，并面临复兴苏维埃的政治竞争，这项任务比以往更加紧迫。代表大会代表的选举本应以新的民主方式进行，但戈尔巴乔夫错误地相信基层会追随他反对机关，没有积极干预，结果党务官僚最终占据多数代表席位。民主苏维埃已在左翼威胁他，现在他又在右翼受到一个强硬保守的代表大会的威胁。
en: In the midst of this process—which Louis XV would have called a deluge—Gorbachev scored his last political victory at the Twenty-eighth Party Congress in early July. The purpose of the Congress was that elusive reform of the apparat which Gorbachev had pursued since he came to power, a task more urgent than ever now that the Party had lost its leading role and had acquired political competition from the revived soviets. The elections of delegates to the Congress were to be conducted in the new democratic manner, but Gorbachev, mistakenly believing that the base would follow his lead against the apparat, did not intervene actively enough, and so the apparatchiki themselves wound up providing the majority of delegates. With the democratic soviets already threatening him on the left, he was now menaced by a militantly conservative Congress on his right.

zh: 6月，这种右翼威胁表现为新成立的俄罗斯共产党。在所有共和国中，只有俄罗斯从未有过单独的党，因为如此庞大组织的规模会自动使它成为全联盟中央党的对手。多年来，这种剥夺一直是一种被压抑的不满，尤其是因为这个据称居帝国统治地位的民族也没有获得给予联盟较小成员的其他共和国“主权”属性——例如单独的科学院。此外，俄罗斯共和国的生活水平低于边疆民族，部分因为土壤较贫瘠、位置偏北，部分因为供应系统组织有缺陷。已经当选联盟代表大会代表的俄罗斯代表抓住这些不满，成立了一个单独的党，戈尔巴乔夫支持这一倡议，因为这样的党将制衡叶利钦的俄罗斯议会。但新的俄罗斯党结果极端保守，它选举改革的死敌伊万·波洛兹科夫为第一书记。由于俄罗斯代表约占联盟代表大会的一半，人们担心代表大会开会时戈尔巴乔夫会有危险。
en: In June this right-wing menace took the form of a newly created Russian Communist Party. Of all the republics, Russia alone had never had a separate Party, because the enormous size of such an organization would have automatically made it a rival to the central, All-Union Party. This deprivation had constituted a suppressed grievance for years, all the more so since the supposedly imperial nation also had none of the other attributes of republic “sovereignty”—a separate Academy of Sciences, for example—accorded to lesser members of the Union. The Russian republic, moreover, had a lower standard of living than the border nations, in part because of its poorer soil and northern location, and in part because of the defective organization of the supply system. The Russian delegates already elected to the Union Congress seized on these grievances to found a separate Party, and Gorbachev went along with this initiative because such a Party would be a counterweight to Yeltsin’s Russian Parliament. But the new Russian Party turned out to be rabidly conservative, and it elected an archfoe of
, one Ivan Polozkov, as its First Secretary. And since the Russian delegates constituted about half of the Union Congress, there was fear that Gorbachev would be in danger when it met.

〔译注〕各共和国生活水平取决于所用指标。世界银行对1990年家庭收入和贫困率的比较显示，波罗的海共和国的相关指标高于俄罗斯，而多个中亚共和国低于俄罗斯，不能笼统概括所有边疆地区。

zh: 然而发生的是戈尔巴乔夫又一次精湛表演：他在右派与左派之间保持平衡，利用每一方对另一方的恐惧，使自己看起来对双方都不可或缺，从而成为所有人近乎一致选择留任总书记的人。一方面，他告诫党务官僚，如果他们想保住党在国家中的领导地位，就必须改革；另一方面，他强调自己的改革意图，以便把民主派留在党内，或至少留在他作为总统的个人领导圈内。“巩固”或团结是他的口号，他借此扭转了保守的代表大会，在秘密投票中获得四分之三的票；因为党务官僚最害怕分裂会摧毁党，并随之摧毁他们自己的地位。
en: What occurred, however, was another virtuoso performance by Gorbachev: he balanced the Right against the Left, playing on each one’s fear of the other to make himself appear indispensable to both, and thus became the near-unanimous choice of all to continue as General Secretary. On the one hand, he lectured the apparatchiki on the need to reform if they wished to preserve the Party’s leading position in the country; on the other hand, he emphasized his own reformist intentions in order to keep the democrats within the Party, or at least within the circle of his personal leadership as president. “Consolidation,” or unity, was his watchword, and with this theme he turned the conservative Congress around, receiving three-quarters of its votes on a secret ballot; for the apparatchiki feared above all a split that would destroy the Party, and with it their own positions.

〔译注〕本段先说“近乎一致”，后说获得四分之三选票；同期报道的结果为3411票赞成、1116票反对。

zh: 与此同时，旧政治局被一个扩大机构取代，其中包括所有十五个共和国的第一书记；这种笨拙的安排意味着戈尔巴乔夫现在在党内拥有集于一身的行政权力。相应地，1988年已经缩减的书记处现在几乎缩减到骨架程度。通过这两项变化，斯大林锻造的党中央政府机构实际上被摧毁。取而代之的是，总统兼总书记依靠一种“个人政治局”——总统委员会（3月成立，他任命了来自左右两派的一组不和谐人物）——以及由如今桀骜不驯的各共和国总统组成的联邦委员会来治理。但这些即兴设立的机构与其说是政府，不如说是一位日益孤立的领导人在不断上涨的洪水中进行的平衡术。因为这最后一次机会的代表大会结果成了最后一次代表大会：在它召开期间，党员人数开始大出血。
en: At the same time, the old Politburo was replaced by an expanded body that included the First Secretaries of all fifteen republics; this unwieldy arrangement meant that Gorbachev now had undivided executive authority within the Party. Accordingly, the Secretariat, already reduced in 1988, was now shrunk to almost skeletal proportions. With these two changes the central institutions of Party government forged by Stalin were in effect destroyed. In their place the president-General Secretary governed with a kind of “personal politburo,” the Presidential Council (which was created in March and to which he appointed a discordant group of figures from both the Right and the Left), and with a Federation Council composed of the presidents of the now rambunctious republics. But these improvised bodies constituted less a government than a permanent balancing act of a now isolated leader amidst the accelerating deluge. For this Congress of the last chance turned out to be the last Congress
while it was taking place, the Party’s membership began a terminal hemorrhage.

zh: 党员流失始于俄罗斯党代表大会。那次集会刺耳的正统主义使改革派成员相信他们别无选择，只能离开；但当叶利钦在联盟代表大会上全国电视直播中辞去党员身份并走出会场时，这一进程获得了全部势头。采取这一行动之前，他警告与会者，如果党不倾听人民的改革意愿，它将失去财产和特权，甚至可能因其劣迹而受审。他退党的借口是，继续留在单一党内与他在全俄罗斯“总统”的职责不相容。更深层的理由是他现在成熟的信念：党无法真正改革，改革只能在党外、并最终反对党来进行。其他主要改革者，如波波夫和索布恰克，立即效仿。简言之，这一时刻标志着改革的终结和真正退出共产主义的开始。
en: The loss of Party members began with the Russian Party Congress. The strident orthodoxy of that assemblage convinced reformist members that they had no choice but to leave; but the process gained its full momentum when, at the Union Congress, Yeltsin resigned his membership on national television and then walked out. Before taking this action he had warned the gathering that if the Party did not heed the popular will for reform, it would lose its property and prerogatives and might even face trial for its misdeeds. The pretext for his resignation was that continued membership in a single Party was incompatible with his obligations as “president” of all of Russia. The deeper reason was his now mature conviction that the Party was incapable of real reform, which could be pursued only outside of, and ultimately against, it. And other leading reformers, such as Popov and Sobchak, immediately followed suit. In short, this moment marked the end of
and the beginning of a genuine exit from Communism.

zh: 在这一转变中，鲍里斯·叶利钦——此前常被莫斯科知识分子和外国政治家同样斥为“特立独行的民粹主义者”，甚至“小丑”——终于得以施展才能。因为现在他在大多数同胞眼中是一位有强烈个人感召力的领袖；而从1990年夏天起，他的领导在苏联戏剧最后一幕的结局中发挥了越来越大的催化作用。
en: In this transition Boris Yeltsin, hitherto often dismissed by Moscow intellectuals and foreign statesmen alike as a “maverick populist,” indeed a “buffoon,” at last came into his own. For he now appeared to most of his compatriots as a genuinely charismatic figure; and his leadership from the summer of 1990 onward played an increasingly catalytic role in the outcome of the last act of the Soviet drama.

zh: 叶利钦成功的一部分原因在于，他从来不是典型的党务官僚。

尽管像戈尔巴乔夫一样是富农被剥夺者的儿子，他的职业生涯并不完全是在机关中从共青团行政逐级升到专职党的工作。相反，他在斯维尔德洛夫斯克工学院受过工程师训练，然后以这一身份在庞大的乌拉尔机械厂（Uralmash）工作，三十二岁成为经理。他两年前入党，主要是因为即使在“现实社会主义”下，非政治生涯也必须入党。他于1976年成为斯维尔德洛夫斯克党委第一书记，很大程度上是因为在苏联环境下，政治权力与他最感兴趣的经济和社会成果的生产可能性密不可分。早些年，他是制度的真诚信仰者，认为通过这个制度可以取得这些成果；然而，他在勃列日涅夫时代的经历使他像同代许多人一样确信，制度阻碍了一切实际改进。于是他成为改革的热烈皈依者，这就是戈尔巴乔夫1986年让他领导莫斯科市机关的原因，结果令人遗憾，我们已看到。
en: A part of Yeltsin’s success was due to the fact that he had never been a classic apparatchik.

Though like Gorbachev he was the son of dekulakized peasants, he had not made his career entirely in the apparat by moving up through Komsomol administration to full-time Party work. Rather, he had been trained as an engineer at the Polytechnic Institute in Sverdlovsk, and then worked in that capacity in the great Urals Machinery Plant (Uralmash) before becoming a manager at age thirty-two. He had joined the Party two years earlier principally because membership was a necessity even for a nonpolitical career under “real socialism.” He became Party First Secretary in Sverdlovsk in 1976 largely because, under Soviet circumstances, political power was inextricably linked to the possibility of producing those economic and social results that interested him most. In his earlier years he was a true-believer in the system and thought those results could be achieved through it; his experience of the Brezhnev era, however, convinced him, like so many others of his generation, that the system thwarted all practical improvement. He thus became an ardent convert to
, and that was why Gorbachev made him head of the Moscow city apparat in 1986, with the sad result that we have seen.

children: 〔译注〕通行传记记载叶利钦曾在建筑系统工作，1963年任住宅建筑联合企业总工程师、1965年任厂长；他于1985年12月而非1986年当选莫斯科市委第一书记。
〔译注〕通行传记记载叶利钦曾在建筑系统工作，1963年任住宅建筑联合企业总工程师、1965年任厂长；他于1985年12月而非1986年当选莫斯科市委第一书记。

zh: 1987年秋叶利钦被机关政治摧毁，显然是他成年生活中的关键事件。他确信制度无法改革；接下来一年半，党的报刊对他大肆辱骂，不给他任何回应机会，这更强化了这一看法。这场磨难还使他与萨哈罗夫一起，成为仅有的两位曾受制度迫害的著名民主领袖；他曾在制度手中受苦，这在许多人眼中有助于保证其信念出于真诚。他显然决心把个人的“政治平反”和把俄罗斯从党中“解放”出来作为毕生使命。随着1989年他以90%的选票当选莫斯科全市代表，他开始长征：先成为俄罗斯议会“主席”，然后成为俄罗斯主权的保护人，最终在1991年成为俄罗斯第一位民主选举的行政首脑。很难看出还有其他俄罗斯民主领袖能完成这样的壮举。
en: Yeltsin’s political destruction at the hands of the apparat in the fall of 1987 was apparently the crucial episode in his mature life. He became convinced that the system could not be reformed, a sentiment that was reinforced when he was vilified for the next year and a half in the Party press, with no opportunity for reply. This ordeal also made him, along with Sakharov, one of just two prominent democratic leaders who had been victims of the system; that he had suffered at its hands helped to guarantee, in the eyes of many people, the honesty of his convictions. He evidently resolved to pursue as his life’s mission both his personal “political rehabilitation” and the “liberation” of Russia from the Party. With his election in 1989 as Moscow deputy-at-large by 90 percent of the vote, he began his long march to become, first, “chairman” of the Russian parliament, then patron of Russian sovereignty, and ultimately, in 1991, Russia’s first democratically elected executive. It is difficult to see how any other Russian democratic leader could have managed such a feat.

zh: 这些经历也使他有可能抛弃党、列宁、社会主义以及制度的所有其他陈词滥调，而戈尔巴乔夫做不到这一点。他的行动在1990年实际上正是这个意思，尽管他的公开言辞不得不更谨慎。于是，随着月份推移，他把自己的激进主义推向逻辑结论，要求经济市场化和私有化。到1990年夏末，叶利钦已拼凑出俄罗斯后改革、实际上后苏联纲领的基础。它由三项原则混合而成：共和国主权原则，即地方控制资源和权力；单独的俄罗斯总统职位（担任这一职务的人很快将由民主选举产生）；以及——我们稍后将更详细看到——向市场和私有财产明确过渡。把这三项原则结合起来，叶利钦当然是在发挥领导作用以加快变革步伐。但更重要的是，他表达了一种当时正随着事态迅速发展而逐渐形成的共识。而没有哪个领域的事态比经济——当时正濒临崩溃——发展得更快、更不祥。
en: And these experiences also made it possible for him, as it was not for Gorbachev, to jettison the Party, Lenin, socialism, and all of the other shibboleths of the system. For this is what his actions in 1990 amounted to, even though his public rhetoric had to be more cautious. Thus, as the months passed he pushed his radicalism to its logical conclusion by demanding the marketization and privatization of the economy. And so by the end of the summer of 1990, Yeltsin had put together the bases of Russia’s post-

, indeed post-Soviet, program. It was compounded of the principles of republic sovereignty, or the local control of resources and power; of a separate Russian presidency (whose occupant would soon be democratically elected); and, as we shall see shortly in greater detail, of an unambiguous transition to the market and private property. In bringing these three principles together, Yeltsin was of course exercising leadership to force the pace of change. But even more, he was articulating a consensus that was now emerging from the rush of events. And in no area were events moving faster or more ominously than in the economy, which was now on the verge of collapse.

zh: 这场危机，如同相关的民族危机和政治制度危机，在1989—1990年冬春突然呈现出压倒性的规模。危机的起源首先是内部的：商品极度短缺，交换退化为物物交换，国家分裂成地方经济单位。这是最根本的危机，因为没有基本生活资料，一切都会崩溃。与此同时，东欧的崩溃戏剧性地表明，这种失败是制度本身的失败，只有改变制度、而非仅仅改革，才能解决。于是，以前禁忌的私有财产和市场观念突然可以公开提倡；到1990年3—4月，政府正积极准备波兰式激进经济过渡的苏联版本。
en: This crisis, like the related crises of the nationalities and of the political system, suddenly assumed overwhelming proportions in the winter and spring of 1989-1990. The origin of the crisis was first of all internal: the scarcity of goods became extreme, exchange degenerated into barter, and the country broke up into local economic units. Here was the most fundamental crisis of all, for without the staff of life everything else would collapse. At the same time, the East European crash dramatized that this failure was one of the system per se, a problem that only a change of system, not a mere reform, could solve. So it suddenly became possible to advocate publicly the previously taboo ideas of private property and the market; and by March-April 1990 the government was actively preparing plans for a Soviet version of the Polish model of radical economic transition.

zh: 但涉及的不仅仅是经济政策的改变。1990年春天发生的是意识革命，不仅在前苏联集团，而且在全世界。突然出现一种普遍共识：市场、私有财产和民主构成一个有机整体；没有个人财产和经济选择自由作为公民社会的物质“基础”，就不可能有法治、人权、宪政和政治多元主义。这一整套东西突然被界定为可行社会——或东欧人现在所说的“正常”社会——唯一可能的形式，与短缺、奴役和结构性低效的异常意识形态世界相对。
en: But more was involved than a change of economic policy. What occurred in the spring of 1990 was a revolution of consciousness, and not just in the former Soviet bloc but throughout the world. There was suddenly a general consensus that the market, private property, and democracy formed an organic whole; that one could not have the rule of law, human rights, constitutional government, and political pluralism without a material “base” for civil society in personal property and freedom of economic choice. This package suddenly came to define the only possible form of a feasible society—or what people in Eastern Europe now called a “normal” society—as opposed to the abnormal ideological world of scarcity, servitude, and structural inefficiency.

zh: 但这场意识革命也意味着社会主义的终结，至少是自1917年以来被理解和实践的完整社会主义的终结。这种社会主义本质上一直是非资本主义，或对私有财产、利润和市场的否定。因此，主张回归这些原则，实质上意味着“恢复资本主义”，而这在苏联对阶级敌人的指控中一直是终极罪行。随着苏联方面承认市场经济的必要性，制度意识形态基础的拆除完成了。于是历史转向了“右”。
en: But this revolution of consciousness also meant the end of socialism, or at least integral socialism as it had been understood and practiced since 1917. This socialism had always been in essence noncapitalism, or the negation of private property, profit, and the market. So the advocacy of returning to these principles in essence meant that “restoration of capitalism” which had always been the ultimate crime in Soviet accusations of the class enemy. With Soviet acceptance of the necessity of a market economy, therefore, the demolition of the ideological basis of the system was complete. And so history moved to the “Right.”

zh: 相应地，1990年春天审查制度逐渐崩溃，然后在6月被合法废除。因为如果能够谈论市场，就能谈论任何事情：索尔仁尼琴的《古拉格群岛》终于在夏天出版；到年底，弗拉基米尔·索洛乌欣以一本名为《读列宁》的小册子违反了终极禁忌，把奠基人还原为有人性、会犯错误的人。
“极权主义”一词现在公开出现在印刷品中，有时甚至由戈尔巴乔夫本人说出。诚然，电视和信息报刊仍属于政权，民主派不得不采取所谓“半萨米兹达特”的诡计，接管专业期刊来发表自己的政治纲领。尽管如此，谎言几乎已经死了。
en: Accordingly, in the spring of 1990 censorship gradually collapsed, and then was legally abolished in June. For if one could talk about the market, one could talk about anything: Solzhenitsyn’s

was at last published in the summer; and by the end of the year Mikhail Soloukhin violated the ultimate taboo with a pamphlet called “Reading Lenin,” in which the Founder was reduced to human and fallible size.

The term “totalitarian” was now openly used in print, and at times was even pronounced by Gorbachev himself. To be sure, television and the informational press still belonged to the regime, and the democrats, in what was called “demi-
,” had to resort to the subterfuge of taking over professional journals to publish their political programs. Nonetheless, the Lie was all but dead.

zh: 基础崩塌：1990年
en: THE BASE CRUMBLES: 1990

zh: 苏联经济崩溃分三个阶段。第一次发生在勃列日涅夫治下，他的停滞加剧了命令-行政制度的结构性缺陷。正如伊戈尔·比尔曼和亚诺什·科尔奈所论证的，苏联型经济按其结构就是一种短缺经济。
在勃列日涅夫治下，如我们所见，越来越复杂的生产体系被包裹在越来越笨重的行政机构中，到1970年代末导致生产下降、质量恶化和技术落后加剧——因而也使企业和消费者都面临短缺。廉价自然资源的耗尽和无法为人们提供工作动力的激励制度进一步加剧了局势。正是这种衰退引发了改革。
en: The Soviet economic breakdown came in three stages. The first occurred under Brezhnev, whose stagnation aggravated the structural defects of the command-administrative system. A Soviet-type economy, as Igor Birman and Janos Kornai have argued, is by its very structure an economy of shortages.

Under Brezhnev, as we have seen, an increasingly complex productive system encased in an increasingly cumbersome administrative apparatus had, by the end of the 1970s, led to declining production, deteriorating quality, and a growing technological lag—and hence also to scarcity for both enterprises and consumers. The situation was further aggravated by the exhaustion of cheap natural resources and by an incentive system that gave no one any motive to work. And it is this declinè that had triggered

〔译注〕苏联1970年代后期经济增长率明显放缓，但按若干统计口径总产出仍在增长；增长放缓与总产出下降并不相同。

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫的补救办法使糟糕局面更加糟糕，而且是分两个阶段。在第一阶段，即经济改革的威权阶段，从1985年到1987年中，对机床和重工业投资的强调增加了消费品短缺；对商品实行“国家验收”或质量控制也减少了生产；反酗酒运动摧毁了有利可图的行业。此外，所有这些花费了大量金钱，第一次使预算赤字问题浮出水面。
en: Gorbachev’s remedies made a bad situation still worse, and they did so in two stages. In the first, or authoritarian, phase of economic

, from 1985 to mid-1987, the emphasis on investment in machine tools and heavy industry increased consumer shortages; “state acceptance,” or quality control, of goods also reduced production; and the anti-alcohol campaign wiped out profitable businesses. All of this, moreover, cost great sums of money, which brought to the surface for the first time the problem of the budget deficit.

zh: 社会主义经济学一直把货币视为不重要的东西，只是便利交换的凭证。因此，自1970年代中期、即大约经济放缓开始以来一直存在赤字这一事实，很少受到注意，以致安德罗波夫从未告诉戈尔巴乔夫。直到1988年10月，政府才承认赤字存在，即使那时也没有表现出太大关切。然而到那时，赤字已因他的政策而从戈尔巴乔夫之前的约占国民生产总值2%至3%上升到约11%。所采取的补救办法是绝望政府的惯用手段：诉诸印钞机。但这种补救，连同日益严重的短缺，促成了第一个五年计划以来未曾见过的另一种现象——通货膨胀；通货膨胀又导致美元作为平行货币的使用日益增加。这一切都没有被预料到，因为这一切本不应在社会主义经济中发生，所以戈尔巴乔夫的经济改革在发展时完全不注意其货币基础。
en: Socialist economics had always treated money as something unimportant, a mere matter of tokens to facilitate exchange. So the fact that there had been a deficit since the mid-1970s, that is, roughly since the economic slowdown began, received so little attention that Andropov never told Gorbachev about it. It was only in October 1988 that the government admitted the deficit existed, and even then it did not show any great concern. Yet by then the deficit, which before Gorbachev had been around 2 to 3 percent of the GNP, had risen, as a result of his policies, to about 11 percent. And the remedy that was adopted was the usual one for desperate governments: the resort to the printing press. But this remedy, in conjunction with the growing shortages, contributed to another phenomenon unknown since the first Five-Year Plan, inflation; and inflation led to the increasing use of the dollar as a parallel currency. None of this had been anticipated because none of this was supposed to occur in socialist economies, so Gorbachev’s economic reform developed without any attention to its monetary base.

〔译注〕苏联在第一个五年计划之后也出现过价格上涨；受管制价格、实际价格和被抑制的通胀须按不同统计口径区分。

zh: 这些财政和货币失衡放大了1987年中至1989年经济改革第二阶段，即自由化阶段的不稳定效应；即使没有这些失衡，这一阶段也足以破坏稳定。首先，新合作社缓解了一些短缺，但也增加了购买力，进而加速了通胀压力；与此同时，合作社与国有部门相互作用，削弱了计划。但最具破坏性的因素是《国有企业法》引入的自我管理和自负盈亏纲领。这一纲领的总效果是摧毁了以前执行计划的垂直指挥链，却没有为生产者、分配者和消费者之间建立市场经济所必需的横向交换渠道。
en: These fiscal and monetary imbalances came to magnify the destabilizing effect of the second, or liberal, phase of economic

, from mid-1987 to 1989, which even without these imbalances would have been destabilizing enough. To begin with, the new cooperatives relieved some shortages but also increased purchasing power, which in turn accelerated inflationary pressure; at the same time, the cooperatives interacted with the state sector to undercut the Plan. But the most disruptive factor of all was the program of self-management and self-financing introduced by the Law on State Enterprises. The overall effect of this program was to destroy the vertical chain of command by which the Plan had previously been carried out, without creating the channels for horizontal exchange among producers, distributors, and consumers that were necessary for a market economy.

zh: 这部法律造成的第一个混乱，来自它分两阶段实施：生产全国一半产出的企业于1988年1月1日转入新制度，另一半则要到次年，从而使经济成为脱节的双轨制。但在改革的第一阶段，企业并没有真正自行其是。在新制度下，企业70%的生产要用于完成国家订单，即

（goszakazy，实际上是旧计划），其余产出则提供给其他客户；这些比例本应每年朝着第二类方向调整。事实上，整个1989年，企业把90%的生产投入国家订单——部分因为国家订单提供了确定市场，部分因为供应仍来自中央物资供应局（Gosnab），部分因为国家计委和各部出于自身利益鼓励这样做。此外，企业常常利用新自由生产旧产品稍作改动的版本，但大幅加价；而且由于有一年经理由工人选举，工厂厂长在紧张的市场中为争夺熟练劳动力而大幅提高工资。于是短缺、通货膨胀和赤字都增加了。
en: The first disruption caused by this law arose from the fact that it was applied in two stages: enterprises producing 50 percent of the national output went over to the new system on January 1, 1988, and the other 50 percent only the following year, thus making the economy a disjointed two-track affair. But in the first stage of the reform, the enterprises did not really strike out on their own. Under the new system, 70 percent of their production was to be devoted to filling state orders, or

(in effect, this was the old Plan), and the rest of their output would be for other customers; these percentages were supposed to shift annually in favor of the second category. In fact, through 1989, enterprises allotted 90 percent of their effort to state orders—in part because these offered a sure market, in part because supplies still came from the central Gosnab, and in part because Gosplan and the ministries, in their own interests, encouraged this. In addition, enterprises often used their new freedom to produce modified versions of their old products but with a large markup; and since for a year managers were elected by the workers, factory directors granted large wage increases in order to compete for skilled labor in a tight market. Thus shortages, inflation, and the deficit all increased.

zh: 与此同时，命令制度的行政机构被大幅削减，这一努力与同时进行的党务机关精简并行。1986年至1989年间，各部、国家计委和国家物资供应局的人员减少了近50%，这意味着企业越来越不得不自谋出路、听凭市场摆布。唯一的麻烦是，并不存在可供它们融入的市场制度。
en: At the same time, the administrative apparatus of the command system was drastically cut, an effort that paralleled the concurrent pruning of the Party apparat. Between 1986 and 1989 the staffs of the ministries, of Gosplan, and of Gosnab were reduced by almost 50 percent, which meant that, willy-nilly, the enterprises were increasingly left to their own devices and to the mercies of the market. The only trouble was that there were no market institutions into which they could integrate themselves.

zh: 工业社会中的市场不能像1921年俄罗斯或1979年中国那些农民主导的社会那样，仅凭一纸命令创造出来：那时，国家只需停止干涉农民生产，让他们把货物运到城里，繁荣就能一夜之间恢复。工业市场需要复杂的批发和零售分销网络、发达的信贷设施，以及一套涵盖从合同到劳动关系的法律；它还需要有纪律的工作习惯、对利润的积极态度，以及承担经过权衡的风险的意愿。建立这样的制度、培育这样的态度需要时间。但苏联政权一直积极阻止所有此类发展；因此，到1989年，当中央行政-命令机构被拆掉一半时，国有企业一脚踏入了虚空。
en: A market in an industrial society cannot be created by simple fiat, as was possible in the peasant-dominated societies of Russia in 1921 or China in 1979: then it had been sufficient for the state to stop interfering with the peasants’ production and to let them take their goods to town in order for prosperity to return overnight. An industrial market requires complex wholesale and retail distribution networks, well-developed credit facilities, and a body of law covering everything from contracts to labor relations; it also requires disciplined habits of work, positive attitudes towards profit, and a willingness to take calculated risks. And it takes time to build such institutions and to nurture such attitudes. But the Soviet regime had actively discouraged all such developments; thus, by 1989, when the central administrative-command apparatus was half-dismantled, the state enterprises stepped out into a void.

zh: 此外，这片虚空由短缺统治——中心不再提供的工业供应、劳动力所需的消费品、城市所需的食品。而所有这些短缺都发生在货币迅速贬值的同时。到1990年，这一切的结果是转向地方配给、以物物交换取代计划，以及国家分裂成力图自给自足的地区单位。每个企业和每个地方都日益囤积它所控制的任何商品。莫斯科和列宁格勒的商店要求顾客出示居住证才肯出售；其他地方实行配给券；工厂用产品交换燃料、原材料或员工所需的消费品；集体农庄拒绝为卢布交出产品，坚持要换取实物商品。与此同时，中心行政系统的崩溃使强迫集体农庄庄员、工人、经理或城市苏维埃维持制度运转成为不可能。的确，经济的解体——专家所说的“细胞化”——只是政治上的主权运动这一制度性分解的另一方面，而这又是权力从大出血的党务机关转移到苏维埃的一个侧面。具有象征意义的是，最后一次党代表大会的年份也是最后一个五年计划的最后一年。这个制度一直是一个整体，其所有部分同时解体只是合乎逻辑的。
en: This void, moreover, was ruled by shortages—of industrial supplies the center no longer provided, of consumer goods for the labor force, and of food for the cities. And all of these shortages occurred at the same time that the currency was rapidly losing its value. By 1990 the result of all this was a transition to rationing on a local basis, barter in place of the Plan, and the breakdown of the country into (would-be) self-sufficient regional units. Each enterprise and each locality increasingly hoarded whatever commodities it controlled. Stores in Moscow and Leningrad demanded to see residence permits before they would sell to customers; other localities introduced ration coupons; factories bartered their products for fuel, raw materials, or consumer goods needed by their employees; kolkhozes refused to part with their produce for rubles and held out for hard goods instead. At the same time, the breakdown of the center’s administrative system made it impossible to coerce kolkhozniks, workers, managers, or city soviets into keeping the system functioning. Indeed, the disintegration—the “cellularization,” as the experts say—of the economy was simply another aspect of the systemic decomposition known in politics as the sovereignty movement, and this in turn was a facet of the transfer of power from the hemorrhaging Party apparat to the soviets. Symbolically, the year of the last Party Congress was also the final year of the last Five-Year Plan. The system had always been of a piece, and it was only logical that all of its parts should disintegrate in unison.

zh: 这种普遍崩溃导致第一次认真努力超越改革的半吊子措施，不是把市场方法嫁接到计划上，而是真正向市场驱动经济过渡。首先，政府再次修订经济改革战略。前一年，即第一次人民代表大会之后，总理雷日科夫任命列昂尼德·阿巴尔金为第一副总理，后者比阿甘别吉扬思想更开放；人们期望政府最终以与危机相称的大胆行动。但阿巴尔金的经济计划被更谨慎的雷日科夫稀释，到1990年初已经过时，于是戈尔巴乔夫转向思想更自由的经济学家尼古拉·彼得拉科夫。然而，作为政府持续犹豫的迹象，当时谈论的是“受管制的市场经济”，换言之，不是真正的东西。尽管如此，3—4月间，政府改革委员会的专家们仍在狂热地起草法令，人们对突破寄予厚望。然后戈尔巴乔夫退缩了，所有这些活动的唯一实际结果是雷日科夫5月底推出的一次拙劣的面包提价，作为尽可能逐步向市场过渡的前奏。各种商品从商店消失，恐慌性抢购席卷全国。
en: This generalized collapse led to the first serious effort to go beyond the half-measures of

and to effect not a graft of market methods onto the Plan, but rather a real transition to a market-driven economy. First, the government once again revised its strategy of economic reform. The previous year, after the First Congress of People’s Deputies, Prime Minister Ryzhkov had made Leonid Abalkin, a more open-minded figure than Aganbegyan, his first deputy; and the expectation was that the government would at last act with a boldness commensurate with the crisis. But Abalkin’s economic plan was watered down by the more cautious Ryzhkov, by early 1990 it was already an anachronism, so Gorbachev turned to the still more liberal-minded economist Nikolai Petrakov. Yet as a sign of the government’s persisting hesitation, the talk was now of a “regulated market economy,” in other words, not of the real thing. Still, in March-April experts of the government’s Reform Commission were feverishly drafting decrees, and expectations were high for a breakthrough. Then Gorbachev drew back, and the only practical result of all this activity was an inept one-time price rise on bread, introduced by Ryzhkov in late May as a prelude to an ever-so-gradual transition to the market. Goods of all kinds disappeared from the stores and panic buying swept the country.

children: 〔译注〕雷日科夫1990年5月宣布面包提价计划后引发抢购；最高苏维埃6月推迟提价，因此提议并非当时已经实施。
〔译注〕雷日科夫1990年5月宣布面包提价计划后引发抢购；最高苏维埃6月推迟提价，因此提议并非当时已经实施。

zh: 主动权随后落到更大胆的人手中。1990年初，在阿巴尔金委员会内部，格里戈里·亚夫林斯基领导的一群年轻经济学家提出了一项休克疗法市场化与私有化计划——结果被戈尔巴乔夫的总统委员会否决。但在6月俄罗斯宣布主权后，叶利钦积极接过这一计划，并任命亚夫林斯基为俄罗斯副总理。面对这种压力，戈尔巴乔夫于8月初与叶利钦和解，两人同意寻求共同经济纲领。于是，戈尔巴乔夫任命了一个由自由派经济学家斯坦尼斯拉夫·沙塔林主持、但实际上由亚夫林斯基推动的新委员会，来设计真正的市场过渡。结果是所谓的“500天计划”，戈尔巴乔夫和叶利钦于8月底大张旗鼓地共同支持：现在看来，国家终于有了一个致力于真正制度转型的团结领导层。叶利钦与戈尔巴乔夫的和解似乎更加彻底，因为他们同意合作，为如今饱受打击的联盟设计新的宪政结构；鉴于各共和国新近要求控制自身资源，这种结构也将与经济改革直接相关。
en: The initiative then passed to bolder hands. At the beginning of 1990, within Abalkin’s Commission, a team of younger economists led by Grigorii Yavlinskii produced a plan for shock-therapy marketization and privatization—only to be turned down by Gorbachev’s Presidential Council. But, after Russia’s declaration of sovereignty in June, Yeltsin aggressively took up this plan and appointed Yavlinskii a deputy prime minister of Russia. Faced with this pressure, Gorbachev made up with Yeltsin in early August and the two agreed to seek a common economic program. Accordingly, Gorbachev appointed a new commission chaired by the liberal economist Stanislav Shatalin, but in fact propelled by Yavlinskii, to devise a real transition to the market. The outcome was the so-called 500-Day Plan, which both Gorbachev and Yeltsin endorsed with fanfare at the end of August: it now seemed as if the country at last had a united leadership committed to genuine transformation of the system. And Yeltsin’s and Gorbachev’s reconciliation seemed all the more complete in that they agreed to cooperate in devising a new constitutional structure for the now battered Union; such a structure would also be directly relevant to economic reform, given the republics’ new pretensions to control their own resources.

zh: 事实上，500天计划既是一份政治文件，也是一份经济文件，因为其条款很难在分配的时间内实施。如果设定如此短的时间框架，是为了使全国感到改革正在推进；经济条款并不打算面面俱到，而是要确定变革的大方向。其中最重要的条款，第一是通过大规模出售政府资产吸收货币过剩来稳定局势，第二是结合大规模私有化迅速引入市场。但该计划最具争议的提议，也许是向各共和国下放征税权，以及对其自然资源、贸易硬通货收入、农业私有化和价格改革管理的控制权。
实际上，500天计划不仅会废除五年计划、解散党，还会解散苏联国家本身。而这正是1990年向左的浪潮一直前进的方向。
en: In fact, the 500-Day Plan was as much a political as an economic document, for its provisions could hardly be implemented in the time allotted. If such a short time-frame was set, it was to give the country a sense of momentum; and the economic provisions were not intended to be comprehensive but to stake out the general direction of movement. The most important of these provisions were, first, the stabilization of the situation by massive sale of government assets to soak up the monetary overhang, and second, the rapid introduction of the market in conjunction with large-scale privatization. But perhaps the plan’s most controversial proposal was to delegate to the republics the power of taxation as well as control over their natural resources, hard currency proceeds from trade, and the administration of agricultural privatization and price reform.

In effect, the 500-Day Plan would dissolve not only the Five-Year Plan and the Party but the Soviet state itself. And this is just the direction in which the leftward surge of 1990 had been heading all along.

zh: 然后，在1990年初秋，这一左倾势头被打断。因为当沙塔林和亚夫林斯基在一座别墅起草他们的计划时，雷日科夫和阿巴尔金在邻近别墅起草了另一份；9月，戈尔巴乔夫把这两份（互不相容的）文件提交最高苏维埃。雷日科夫-阿巴尔金计划虽然确实规定向市场过渡，但提议用五年而非500天达到目标；而且它不向各共和国下放任何权力。戈尔巴乔夫起初呼吁对这两个计划进行“综合”，并请回阿甘别吉扬来完成——实际上是要化圆为方，戈尔巴乔夫对此心知肚明。随后他拒绝了由此产生的妥协，进一步后退，说服最高苏维埃给他三周时间综合此时已经出现的三个计划。10月，实际批准的只是沙塔林计划的若干笼统内容和关于“深入改革”的空洞套话。随着500天计划被这样搁置，改革实际上已经死了，尽管几个月后这一点才会显现。戈尔巴乔夫现在发现自己越来越在捍卫现状。
en: Then in the early fall of 1990, this leftward momentum was broken. For while Shatalin and Yavlinskii had been drafting their plan in one dacha, in a neighboring dacha Ryzhkov and Abalkin had been drafting another; and Gorbachev put the two (incompatible) documents before the Supreme Soviet in September. Although the Ryzhkov-Abalkin plan indeed provided for a transition to the market, it proposed taking five years, not five hundred days, to get there; and it delegated no powers to the republics. Gorbachev at first called for a “synthesis” of these two plans and he brought back Aganbegyan to produce it—in effect to square a circle, as Gorbachev well knew. He then turned down the resulting compromise and retreated still further by persuading the Supreme Soviet to give him three weeks to synthesize what were now three plans. In October, all that was actually approved were a few generalities from the Shatalin plan and airy platitudes about “deep reforms.” With this scuttling of the 500-Day Plan
was in fact dead, although this would not become apparent until several months later. Gorbachev now found himself increasingly defending the status quo.

zh: 当时，戈尔巴乔夫10月的后退在许多人看来又是他的一次战术撤退，旨在安抚右派，然后再向前推进。大多数民主派仍希望以“左中联盟”解决日益加深的危机。事实上，他们第一次看到了真正的戈尔巴乔夫。500天计划如果实施，将拆解制度，而这正是叶利钦和计划发起者想要的。但戈尔巴乔夫一如既往全神贯注于政治——党代表大会、联盟条约和德国统一——太晚才意识到沙塔林计划的革命含义，于是在看似实施的同时破坏了它。
en: At the time, Gorbachev’s October backtracking appeared to many as yet another of his tactical retreats designed to buy off the Right before moving forward again. Most democrats still hoped for a “Left-center coalition” as a solution to the deepening crisis. In fact, for the first time they had encountered the real Gorbachev. The 500-Day Plan, if implemented, would have dismantled the system, and that was just what Yeltsin and the plan’s sponsors desired. But Gorbachev, as ever preoccupied with politics—the Party Congress, the Union Treaty, and German reunification—realized the Shatalin plan’s revolutionary implications only belatedly, and so sabotaged it while appearing to put it into effect.

zh: 因为当关键时刻到来时，他不能接受放弃“社会主义财产”，也不能接受市场的主导地位或联盟内真正的权力下放。还必须补充，他也不能接受自己“总统”权力的缩小。简言之，尽管说了那么多革命变革的话，戈尔巴乔夫始终只是一个改革共产主义者，尽管是非常先进的一种。更准确地说，他是一个从未理解制度性质对改革所施加结构性限制的改革共产主义者。于是，他轻率地把改组推到不可修复地“解构”制度的程度，然后当阻止他所召唤的力量为时已晚时才后退。于是，像巫师学徒一样，他在剩余掌权时间里试图驾驭自己释放的洪水。
en: For when the chips were down, he could not accept the abandonment of “socialist property,” the sovereignty of the market, or a real devolution of power within the Union. Nor, it must be added, could he accept the diminution of his own “presidential” power. In short, for all his rhetoric about revolutionary change, Gorbachev had never been anything more than a Reform Communist, albeit of a very advanced sort. Or more exactly, he was a Reform Communist who had never understood the structural limitations on reform imposed by the nature of the system. So he rashly pushed restructuring to the point where he had irreparably “destructured” the system and then drew back when it was too late to stop the forces he had conjured up. So, like the sorcerer’s apprentice, he would spend the rest of his time in power trying to ride the deluge he had unleashed.

zh: 反动与崩溃：1990年9月—1991年12月
en: REACTION AND COLLAPSE: SEPTEMBER 1990-DECEMBER 1991

zh: 因此，戈尔巴乔夫时代的最后一年——从1990年10月的后退到1991年8月的政变——本质上是改革和苏联现象本身的一段漫长尾声。与民主派的经济计划决裂后，戈尔巴乔夫被迫越来越依赖旧建制，而旧建制此时正处于强硬反对夏天激进突破的情绪中。这反过来只能使民主派进一步激进化，从而为最终以政变告终的力量摊牌搭好舞台。
en: Thus the last year of the Gorbachev era—from the October retreat of 1990 to the August putsch of 1991—is essentially a long epilogue to

and to the Soviet phenomenon itself. Having broken with the economic plans of the democrats, Gorbachev was forced to rely increasingly on the old establishment, which was now in a mood of militant reaction against the radical breakthrough of the summer. And this, in turn, could only further radicalize the democrats, and thereby set the stage for the showdown test of strength that would culminate in the putsch.

zh: 如果戈尔巴乔夫10月的后退从根本上说是信念问题，那么这一信念又被务实的权力算计所强化。
因为尽管民主派此时被舆论力量推着走，国家的真正权力仍掌握在党务机关、克格勃、军队和军工复合体手中，后者控制着国家近一半的经济，可能雇用了三分之一劳动力。这些权力中心越来越清楚地向戈尔巴乔夫表明，如果他不阻止民主派，他们就会代他动手。为了保住自己的位置，他顺从了。
en: If Gorbachev’s October retreat was at bottom a matter of conviction, this conviction was reinforced by pragmatic calculations of power.

For, though the democrats were now carried forward by the strength of public opinion, the real power in the country remained with the Party apparat, the KGB, the army, and the military-industrial complex, which controlled nearly half of the country’s economy and employed probably one third of its work force. And these centers of power made it increasingly clear to Gorbachev that if he did not halt the democrats, they would do so in his place. So to keep his place he went along.

zh: 9月，莫斯科周围神秘的军队调动被广泛解读为警告戈尔巴乔夫改变路线。10月，与军工复合体领导人的紧张会晤，以及瓦西里·斯塔罗杜布采夫新成立的“农民联盟”（代表约三百万集体农庄官僚）的压力，帮助说服戈尔巴乔夫埋葬了500天计划。11月，与一千多名军官召开的激烈会议使他确信保守派已接近沸点。相应地，12月初，他用前克格勃将军鲍里斯·普戈取代自由派内务部长瓦季姆·巴卡京。12月晚些时候，温和改革者雷日科夫被挤下总理职位，1月由死硬的老派经济学家瓦连京·帕夫洛夫接替。在最后一次人事变动中，12月戈尔巴乔夫迫使不情愿的人民代表大会选举无能的根纳季·亚纳耶夫为副总统。与此同时，国家广播电视被置于一位只对戈尔巴乔夫负责的保守官员之下；1月，《观点》节目被关闭，戈尔巴乔夫还试图废除前一年的新闻自由法。正是在这些变化之中，12月底，谢瓦尔德纳泽戏剧性地辞职，并发出含义难明的警告：“独裁即将到来”。果然，斯塔罗杜布采夫、普戈、帕夫洛夫和亚纳耶夫都将出现在8月政变的领导人中。
en: In September, mysterious army maneuvers around Moscow had been widely interpreted as a warning to Gorbachev to change course. In October, tense meetings with leaders of the military-industrial complex, and pressure from Vasilii Starodubtsev’s new “Peasant Union,” which represented some three million kolkhoz bureaucrats, helped persuade Gorbachev to bury the 500-Day Plan. In November, stormy sessions with more than one thousand army officers convinced him that the conservatives were nearing the boiling point. Accordingly, in early December he replaced the liberal interior minister Vadim Bakatin with the former KGB general Boris Pugo. Later in December, the tepid reformer Ryzhkov was eased out as prime minister, to be replaced in January by the die-hard, old-line economist Valentin Pavlov. In a final personnel change, in December Gorbachev forced a reluctant Congress of People’s Deputies to elect the incompetent Gennadii Yanaiev as vice president. At the same time, state radio and television were placed under a conservative official responsible to Gorbachev alone; in January the program

was closed down, and Gorbachev sought to repeal the law on press freedom of the previous year. It was in the midst of these changes, in late December, that Shevardnadze dramatically resigned with an enigmatic warning against the “onset of dictatorship.” And, indeed, Starodubtsev, Pugo, Pavlov, and Yanaiev would all show up among the leaders of the August coup.

zh: 1991年1月中旬，这场逐步推进的政变开始付诸行动，对立陶宛和拉脱维亚的通信设施发动血腥军事攻击。这些行动的意图似乎是镇压这些麻烦的分离主义共和国，以此作为在中央镇压的前奏，因为2月士兵被派去巡逻莫斯科街道。与此同时，帕夫洛夫用近乎斯大林主义的语言声称，西方经济援助是摧毁苏联社会主义阴谋的一部分；而克格勃首脑克留奇科夫则指责中央情报局通过鼓动市场来密谋颠覆共产主义制度。同时，帕夫洛夫没收了所有面额五十卢布以上的钞票，表面上是为了减少货币过剩；戈尔巴乔夫则赋予克格勃全权，通过搜查包括合资企业在内的所有商业办事处来打击“经济犯罪”；很可能这些都是一项僵硬的国家经济控制计划的笨拙前奏，该计划旨在配合已经在进行的警察行动。然后，莫名其妙地，所有这些活动都停止了，仿佛其执行者不敢贯彻到底。
en: In mid-January 1991, what was by now a creeping coup d’état went into action with bloody military attacks against the communications facilities in Lithuania and Latvia. The intention behind these actions seems to have been to put down these troublesome secessionist republics as a prelude to cracking down in the center, for in February soldiers were assigned to patrolling the streets of Moscow. At the same time, using almost Stalinist language, Pavlov claimed that Western economic aid was part of a plot to destroy Soviet socialism; meanwhile, KGB chief Kriuchkov accused the CIA of conspiring to subvert the Communist system through agitation for the market. Simultaneously, Pavlov confiscated all bills larger than fifty rubles, ostensibly to reduce the monetary overhang, and Gorbachev gave the KGB full powers to fight “economic crime” by searching all business offices, including joint ventures; it is quite likely that these were an inept prelude to a program of rigid state economic controls designed to accompany the police actions already in progress. Then, unaccountably, all of this activity stopped, as if its perpetrators did not dare to follow through.

zh: 尽管如此，保守派的活动已足以引发民主派的新动员：十多万示威者在莫斯科街头抗议波罗的海国家的流血事件，叶利钦无疑认为自己会是旧卫队的下一个目标，于是呼吁戈尔巴乔夫辞职，甚至呼吁民主派向总统“宣战”。他

是下一个目标，因为3月俄罗斯议会中占相对多数的共产党人试图弹劾主席叶利钦。然而，这一策略被挫败了：他成功号召支持者于3月28日举行大规模示威，直接违抗戈尔巴乔夫的禁令，而该禁令有五万军队作为后盾。尽管如此，仍有数十万人集会，这一天在没有暴力的情况下结束，成为民主派的政治胜利。此时，较量已远远超出莫斯科：西伯利亚煤田和白俄罗斯工厂的罢工者表示支持叶利钦，要求戈尔巴乔夫辞职；后者则谴责其对手的“布尔什维克”街头战术。
en: Nonetheless, the conservatives’ activity had sufficed to produce a new mobilization of the democrats: over a hundred thousand demonstrators protested in Moscow’s streets against the bloodshed in the Baltic states, and Yeltsin, no doubt thinking he would be the old guard’s next target, called for Gorbachev’s resignation and even for a “declaration of war” by the democrats against the president. And indeed he

the next target, for in March the Communist plurality in the Russian parliament attempted to impeach Yeltsin as chairman. This strategy was thwarted, however, when he successfully called for a massive demonstration of his supporters on March 28 in direct defiance of a ban by Gorbachev, a ban backed up by fifty thousand troops. Several hundred thousand people assembled nonetheless, and the day ended without violence in a political victory for the democrats. And by this time the sparring extended well beyond Moscow: strikers in the Siberian coal fields and the Bielorussian factories expressed support for Yeltsin and called for Gorbachev’s resignation, while the latter reacted by denouncing the “Bolshevik” street tactics of his opponents.

zh: 但三月危机最重要的结果是设立了俄罗斯总统职位，担任这一职务的人将由普选产生。这一发展又与当年春天发生的另一个进程密切相关，即戈尔巴乔夫寻求新的联盟条约。从1988年纳戈尔内卡拉巴赫爆发到1990年初立陶宛宣布独立，戈尔巴乔夫一直把民族问题当作次要问题。但他终于被1990年夏天的“主权游行”吓得采取行动，从那时起，拯救联盟成为他的首要关切，远远超过经济改革。
en: But the most important result of the March crisis was the creation of a Russian presidency whose occupant would be chosen by universal suffrage. And this development was intimately linked with another process transpiring that spring, namely Gorbachev’s quest for a new Union Treaty. From the eruption of Nagornyi Karabakh in 1988 until Lithuania’s declaration of independence in early 1990, Gorbachev had treated the nationalities as a secondary problem. But he was at last frightened into action by the “parade of sovereignties” of the summer of 1990, and from that time onward saving the Union was his primary preoccupation, far ahead of economic reform.

zh: 到1990年11月，他已拟订新联盟条约草案，以取代1922年的成立文件。草案提议把国名改为“主权苏维埃共和国联盟”，但实质上把大部分真正权力保留在中心。由于各共和国不接受，他试图通过组织1991年3月17日全民公决来削弱它们。公决要求选民批准把联盟保留为“平等苏维埃共和国革新的联邦”——措辞如此含糊，很难说不。作为对这一自认为聪明之举的回应，叶利钦做了一件真正聪明的事：他说服俄罗斯议会在戈尔巴乔夫的公决中附加自己关于设立普选俄罗斯总统的单独问题。戈尔巴乔夫的公决获得70%苏联选民批准，而叶利钦的公决获得85%俄罗斯选民批准。面对这种压力，俄罗斯人民代表大会把总统选举定在6月12日。
en: By November 1990 he had the draft of a new Union Treaty to replace the founding document of 1922. It proposed changing the country’s name to Union of Sovereign Soviet Republics but essentially retained most of the real power at the center. Since this was not acceptable to the republics, he tried to undercut them by organizing a referendum for March 17, 1991. It asked voters to approve the preservation of the Union as a “renewed federation of equal Soviet republics”—language so vague it would be difficult to say no. In response to this would-be clever move, Yeltsin made a genuinely clever one: he persuaded the Russian parliament to append to Gorbachev’s referendum its own separate question on the establishment of a popularly elected Russian president. Gorbachev’s referendum was approved by 70 percent of the Soviet voters, whereas Yeltsin’s referendum received the approval of 85 percent of Russian voters. Faced with this pressure, the Russian Congress of People’s Deputies set the presidential election for June 12.

〔译注〕苏联全联盟公决约76%的投票者支持保留革新后的联盟；俄罗斯增设总统职位的单独问题约69.85%的投票者赞成。几个共和国的政府抵制了全联盟公决。

zh: 在3月叶利钦及其民主派战胜爬行政变第二阶段之后，戈尔巴乔夫4月不得不向左转回。仍在寻求新联盟条约的他，与尚未宣布打算分离的九个共和国领导人进行秘密谈判，叶利钦及其同事在这些谈判中处于有利地位。这些讨论大致相当于苏联版的波兰“圆桌”，民主派明确指出了这一相似之处。
en: After the March victory of Yeltsin and his democrats against the second phase of the creeping coup d’état, Gorbachev in April had to double back to the Left. Still in pursuit of a new Union Treaty, he entered into secret negotiations with the leaders of the nine republics that had not declared their intention of seceding, negotiations in which Yeltsin and his colleagues held the strong hand. These discussions were roughly the Soviet equivalent of the Polish “round table,” a parallel the democrats explicitly drew.

zh: 由此产生的“9+1”协议虽然在形式上是妥协，但给予九方的远多于一方。戈尔巴乔夫获得了对“劳动纪律”的呼吁以稳定经济，以及最近支持叶利钦的罢工的结束。但九方获得了对波罗的海和高加索共和国分离权的默许，这也是其余共和国真正主权的保证；这一点通过向所有成员共和国转移重大经济和行政权力，以及承诺在1992年前制定新宪法并在全联盟进行真正民主选举而得到明确。此外，俄罗斯获得了其境内所有矿山的所有权、单独的克格勃，以及独立的电视台，后者终于打破了政府对最重要媒体的垄断。
en: The resulting “9-plus-1” agreement, although formally a compromise, gave far more to the 9 than to the 1. Gorbachev obtained a call for “work discipline” to stabilize the economy, and the end of the strikes that had recently supported Yeltsin. But the 9 obtained implicit acceptance of the Baltic and the Caucasian republics’ right to secede, which was also the guarantee of real sovereignty for those that remained; this was spelled out by the transfer of significant economic and administrative power to all member republics, and by the promise of a new constitution and genuinely democratic elections throughout the Union by 1992. In addition, Russia received ownership of all mines on its territory; a separate KGB; and an independent television, which at last broke the government’s monopoly of the most important of the media.

zh: 下个月，民主派巩固了胜利：叶利钦以公开反共纲领在俄罗斯各地竞选后，在6月12日选举中大获全胜。他在第一轮就以57%的选票击败两名共产党候选人——保守的雷日科夫和自由派的巴卡京，后者被推出来分散选票、迫使叶利钦进入第二轮——而极右候选人弗拉基米尔·日里诺夫斯基获得7%。一场市政投票把列宁格勒改回圣彼得堡，象征性地凸显了这场选举的革命含义。6月12日的结果意味着，现在明显处于少数的共产党人失去权力只是时间问题。于是他们发动了当年第三次政变企图。
en: The next month the democrats consolidated their victory when Yeltsin, after stumping Russia with an overtly anti-Communist program, won the June 12 elections hands down. He did so on the first round with 57 percent of the vote against two Communist candidates, the conservative Ryzhkov and the liberal Bakatin, who had been fielded to split the vote and force Yeltsin into a run-off, while the far-right candidate Vladimir Zhirinovskii received 7 percent. The revolutionary import of the election was driven home symbolically by a municipal vote to change the name of Leningrad back to St. Petersburg. The outcome of June 12 meant that it was merely a question of time before the Communists, now clearly in the minority, would lose power. Thus they launched their third coup attempt of the year.

zh: 6月底，帕夫洛夫在最高苏维埃要求把通常属于总统的法令权转交给他本人。同时，亚佐夫、克留奇科夫和普戈在立法机构的一次闭门会议上说，国家面临迫在眉睫的灾难，并明显暗示戈尔巴乔夫应负责。虽然这是近乎煽动叛乱的抗命，戈尔巴乔夫作出的最强硬回应不过是到议会面前，对代表们发表一通激烈讲话，劝他们拒绝帕夫洛夫的要求。但没有人被逮捕，甚至没有人被解职。戈尔巴乔夫显然已失去对局势和自己政府的控制；更糟的是，他似乎并不知道这一点。于是，他梦游般走入8月的最后摊牌。
en: In late June Pavlov went before the Supreme Soviet and demanded that the decree powers normally held by the president be transferred to himself. At the same time, Yazov, Kriuchkov, and Pugo told a closed session of the legislature that the country faced an imminent disaster, and they clearly implied that Gorbachev was responsible. Though this was insubordination verging on sedition, Gorbachev came up with nothing more forceful in response than to appear before parliament to harangue the deputies into refusing Pavlov’s demands. But no one was arrested or even fired. Gorbachev had clearly lost control of the situation and of his own government; even worse, he did not seem to know it. And so he sleepwalked into the final showdown of August.

zh: 在此过程中，并在叶利钦的持续压力下，戈尔巴乔夫于7月底同意把9+1协议的承诺扩展为一份激进分权的联盟条约草案。这份文件把征税权以及保留部分税收的权力让给共和国，只把一部分上缴中心。于是，戈尔巴乔夫为拯救联盟而寻求新条约的努力，结果却规定了联盟的近乎解体；他把该文件的签署日期定在8月20日。随后他前往伦敦参加主要工业国七国集团峰会，希望推动一项“大交易”或马歇尔计划，让西方援助确保一个稳定的俄罗斯。他空手而归，地位进一步削弱。
en: Along the way, and under continuing pressure from Yeltsin, Gorbachev in late July agreed to expand the promises of the 9-plus-1 agreement into a draft of a radically decentralizing Union Treaty. This document conceded to the republics the authority to collect taxes and to retain a portion thereof, turning over only a share to the center. Thus Gorbachev’s quest for a new Treaty, undertaken to save the Union, wound up providing for its near dissolution; and he scheduled the signing of this document for August 20. He then departed to London for a summit of the seven leaders of the major industrial states, the G-7, in the hope of promoting a “grand bargain,” or Marshall plan, whereby Western aid would secure a stable Russia. His position was weakened further when he came back empty-handed.

zh: 回国后，他为挽救局势作了最后一次尝试，寻求把党改造成一个准社会民主组织。在最后一次精湛表演中——他向来口才很好——戈尔巴乔夫说服中央委员会会议批准一个新党纲，抛弃马克思列宁主义，转向含糊的“人道民主社会主义”，仿佛凭几句公式化的话使党在临终前转变就能改变国家局面。这是1989年匈牙利和其他东欧党的策略，当时没有用，现在也同样没有用。
en: On his return home he made his last attempt to save the situation by seeking to transform the Party into a quasi-social-democratic organization. In a final bravura performance—he always spoke well—Gorbachev persuaded a meeting of the Central Committee to endorse a new Party platform that jettisoned Marxism-Leninism in favor of a vague “humane and democratic socialism,” as if such a deathbed conversion of the Party by verbal formula would make a difference to the country. This was the tactic of the Hungarian and the other East European Parties in 1989, and it worked no better now than it had then.

zh: 正是7月的这些让步引发了8月的最后政变企图。虽然其开始日期8月19日无疑是因为新联盟条约原定20日签署，但其真正动机是阻止自6月选举、甚至自1990年夏天500天计划以来一直逼近的这一制度的覆灭。因此，这是一次迟来的绝望行动，在此前三番犹豫不决的尝试之后笨拙地实施，执行者已不再相信自己有真正成功的机会。
en: It is these concessions of July that provoked the final coup attempt in August. Although its beginning date, August 19, was no doubt determined by the fact that the new Union Treaty was to have been signed on the 20th, its real motivation was to stave off the defeat of the system that had been looming since the June elections, indeed since the 500-Day Plan of the summer of 1990. As such, it was a belated act of desperation, ineptly carried out after three previous and hesitant attempts, by people who no longer believed they stood a real chance.

zh: “政变总参谋部”已就位数月：除了已经提到的名字，只需再加上国防委员会的奥列格·巴克拉诺夫，即军工复合体，以及戈尔巴乔夫私人办公室主任瓦列里·博尔金。简言之，这场政变不是几个偶然出现的“政变阴谋者”的行动；它是苏联政府本身的行动，是为捍卫现有共产主义建制而实施的。其最初目标是迫使戈尔巴乔夫宣布紧急状态，并通过镇压叶利钦和民主派来“恢复秩序”。其领导人大概相信，戈尔巴乔夫面临否定他们的行动会给国家带来的危险，会加入他们。此外，紧急状态选项在政府中已考虑很久，戈尔巴乔夫不可能感到意外。然而，当阴谋者拿着待签的紧急状态法令面对他时，他退却了，回答说此事应提交最高苏维埃。于是他们决定废黜他，让副总统取而代之，并由自己宣布紧急状态。但这一行动准备不足。军队和克格勃没有像政府期望的那样顺从命令；因此叶利钦和民主派有时间组织抵抗，在三天内使阴谋者的意志崩溃，政权也随之崩溃。因此，8月政变在可比的意义上类似于1917年科尔尼洛夫将军的失败行动：它表明右派没有力量，从而让左派以革命方式冲上前去摧毁旧秩序。
en: The “general staff of the coup had been in place for months: to the names already mentioned it is only necessary to add Oleg Baklanov of the Defense Council, that is, the military-industrial complex, and Valerii Boldin, the chief of Gorbachev’s personal cabinet. In short, the coup was not an action of some adventitious “coup plotters”; it was an action of the Soviet government itself, and was carried out in defense of the existing Communist establishment. Its initial aim was to force Gorbachev to declare a state of emergency and to “restore order” by putting down Yeltsin and the democrats. Its leaders probably believed that Gorbachev, faced with the dangers to the state of repudiating their initiative, would join them. Moreover, the option of a state of emergency had been under consideration in the government for a long time and could hardly come as a surprise to Gorbachev. Nonetheless, when he was confronted by the conspirators with the emergency decree to be signed, he backed off with the answer that the matter should be referred to the Supreme Soviet. So they decided to depose him in favor of his vice president and to declare the emergency themselves. But the move had been inadequately prepared. The army and the KGB did not dutifully follow orders as the government expected; thus Yeltsin and the democrats had time to organize a resistance that in three days produced the collapse of the conspirators’ will, and with it the collapse of the regime. Thus the August putsch was, mutatis mutandis, analogous to General Kornilov’s failed action in 1917: it demonstrated that the Right had no force, and so permitted the Left to rush forward in revolutionary fashion to destroy the old order.

zh: 叶利钦和民主派一方也有准备和真正的政治意志。戈尔巴乔夫早先把他们比作布尔什维克，并非完全错误，因为面对政府的“军政府”，民主派发动了一场实际上的反政变，以确保制度彻底崩溃。冬天与毁灭擦肩而过使他们警觉，而他们自己过去作为党员的经历又使他们了解对手的运作方式，因此他们事先就为8月遇到的这种突发情况作了准备：他们唯一不知道的是具体日期。
en: And there was preparation and a real political will on the side of Yeltsin and the democrats. Gorbachev had not been entirely wrong in comparing them earlier to the Bolsheviks, for in response to the governmental “junta” the democrats mounted what was in effect a countercoup to insure that the system did collapse completely. Alerted by their near-brush with doom during the winter, and enlightened about their adversaries’ mode of operation by their own past as Party members, they had prepared in advance for just such a contingency as the one they encountered in August: all they did not know was the date.

zh: 他们的策略是，首先严格在新建立的苏联法治国家（
）框架内行动，声称只为捍卫宪法和恢复戈尔巴乔夫的合法权威而工作。然而，他们更基本的策略是利用自己在俄罗斯共和国的权力基地——其新克格勃、选举中支持叶利钦的军队单位，以及部长会议和相关人员——把俄罗斯联邦的“白宫”变成挫败政变者即苏联政府的指挥所。这一策略在政变第二天成功后，他们利用危机拆解党国，而这始终是他们的真正目标。
en: Their strategy was, first, to act scrupulously within the framework of the new Soviet

, claiming to work only for the defense of the constitution and the restoration of the legitimate authority of Gorbachev. Their more basic strategy, however, was to use their power base in the Russian republic—its new KGB, the army units that had supported Yeltsin in the elections, and its Council of Ministers together with related staff—to turn the Russian Federation’s “White House” into a command post for thwarting the putschists—that is, the Soviet government. Once this strategy had succeeded, on the second day of the coup, they exploited the crisis in order to dismantle the Party-state, which had been their real aim all along.

zh: 他们成功了，因为他们在关键地方拥有民众支持。诚然，叶利钦第一天呼吁莫斯科民众举行总罢工失败了。但这很大程度上是因为街头有坦克，人们相信苏联政府已经赢了——它过去总是赢——党员们急忙补缴拖欠的党费。然而，一旦叶利钦的抵抗表明政变失败，首都和圣彼得堡民众的真实感情便在欣喜若狂的解放浪潮中公开迸发。虽然这些情绪在大城市中心最为明显——这些城市自1989年以来投票支持民主派（各省仍基本被动）——但毫无疑问，人口中政治上活跃的分子支持叶利钦的反政变。捷尔任斯基纪念碑被拆除，列宁雕像开始倒下，红旗被1917年临时政府的三色旗取代，老广场的中央委员会总部被俄罗斯联邦政府查封。于是，叶利钦和民主派在表面上捍卫现有苏联秩序的同时，实际上颠覆了它；以维护政治连续性的名义，他们进行了一场革命。
en: And they succeeded because they had popular support where it counted. To be sure, Yeltsin’s appeal on the first day to the Moscow population for a general strike failed. But this was largely because with tanks in the streets people believed that the Soviet government had already won—as it always had in the past—and Party members anxiously started paying up back dues. Yet once Yeltsin’s resistance had demonstrated the coup’s failure, the real feelings of the populations of the capital and St. Petersburg burst out in the open in a euphoric rush to liberation. Although these sentiments were most marked in the large urban centers that since 1989 had voted for the democrats (the provinces remained largely passive), there can be no doubt that the politically active elements of the population supported Yeltsin’s countercoup. The Dzerzhinskii monument was toppled, the Lenin statues started coming down, the red flag was replaced by the tricolor of the Provisional Government of 1917, and the Central Committee headquarters on Old Square was sequestered by the government of the Russian Federation. Thus Yeltsin and the democrats, in ostensibly defending the existing Soviet order, in fact subverted it; in the guise of preserving political continuity they made a revolution.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫回到莫斯科后的行为，完成了使这一制度和他本人失去信誉的任务。首先，他没有立即去白宫感谢救他的人，而是打电话给西方各国元首，告知自己获救。第二，他没有去俄罗斯议会，而是召开新闻发布会，不谈国家，只谈自己在政变期间的个人磨难。最后，他没有注意到国家在政变三天里已完全改变，反而断言共产党对改革的进一步推进仍然不可或缺。因此，当他终于拜访叶利钦和议会时，迎接他的是敌意的呼喊，说党是“犯罪企业”；叶利钦让他宣读其部长会议批准政变的会议记录；俄罗斯总统随后炫耀性地签署一项显然事先准备好的法令，中止该党在俄罗斯全境的活动。这些电视转播的场面在西方公众中反响不佳，他们仍认为戈尔巴乔夫掌权，并认为在被西方误判为“未遂政变”（而非革命）之后，改革会照旧进行。但在俄罗斯，电视上的对抗效果很好，因为民众确实愤慨：戈尔巴乔夫的改革把国家带到如此低谷，而他又完全不明白发生了什么。
en: Gorbachev’s behavior upon his return to Moscow completed the task of discrediting the system, and his person. First, he did not go immediately to thank his saviors at the White House, but instead telephoned his fellow heads of state in the West to inform them of his deliverance. Second, he did not go to the Russian parliament, but instead called a press conference where he talked not of the country but only of his personal ordeal during the coup. Finally, he failed to notice that the country had changed completely during the three days of the coup, and instead asserted that the Communist Party remained indispensable to the further progress of

. So when he at last visited Yeltsin and the parliament, he was met with hostile cries that the Party was “a criminal enterprise”; Yeltsin made him read the minutes of his Council of Ministers approving the coup; and the Russian president then ostentatiously signed a decree—obviously prepared in advance—suspending the Party throughout Russia. These televised proceedings went over badly with the Western public, which still thought that Gorbachev was in charge and that after what the West misjudged as a “failed coup” (not a revolution)
would proceed as before. But in Russia the televised confrontation played very well, for the population was genuinely indignant that Gorbachev’s
had brought the country so low and that he failed so completely to understand what had happened.

zh: 因此，戈尔巴乔夫虽然名义上恢复掌权，实际上此时只是傀儡，甚至可以说某种人质，叶利钦和民主派随后利用他为制度主要机构的清算提供法律基础。首先，他被告知任命叶利钦的人选担任国防部长和克格勃首脑，经济控制权从他手中拿走，交给俄罗斯总理。当国家已根本改变的认知终于渗入他的头脑时，戈尔巴乔夫解散了中央委员会并辞去总书记职务。接着，他被用作总统来策划联盟最高苏维埃和人民代表大会的自我清算——从而摧毁他自己的重大改革。与此同时，所有尚未宣布独立的共和国都宣布独立，实际上解散了联盟。对这个制度的最后一击发生在10月底，叶利钦以法令把他对共产党的中止变成永久禁令，并没收了党的全部财产。
en: Thus, although nominally restored to power, Gorbachev was in fact now only a figurehead, indeed something of a hostage, whom Yeltsin and the democrats then used to give a legal basis to the liquidation of the main institutions of the system. First, he was told to appoint Yeltsin candidates to the posts of minister of defense and head of the KGB, and control of the economy was taken from him and put under the Russian prime minister. When realization that the country had fundamentally changed at last sunk in, Gorbachev dissolved the Central Committee and resigned as General Secretary. Next, he was employed as president to engineer the self-liquidation of the Union’s Supreme Soviet and the Congress of Peoples’ Deputies—thus demolishing his own major reform. At the same time, all the republics that had not yet done so declared their independence, thus in fact dissolving the Union. The final blow to the system came in late October, when Yeltsin, by decree, transformed his suspension of the Communist Party into a permanent ban and confiscated all of the Party’s property.

zh: 在这场革命完成之前，只剩下两件大事需要清理：第一，苏联国家仍然形式存在，它是庞大核武库的名义拥有者，以及众多国际协定的签署方。第二，这个国家的“总统”仍顽固地幻想自己还在执政，而这种幻想在外国首都甚至更强烈。
en: There remained only two major matters to be cleared up before this revolution would be complete: first, there was the still formal existence of a Soviet state, the titular possessor of an enormous nuclear arsenal and the signatory of numerous international obligations. Second, there was the persistent illusion of that state’s “president” that he still governed, an illusion even more strongly held in foreign capitals.

zh: 表面上看，以某种形式保留联盟的政治框架似乎是合理的，以便提供统一的经济空间、充当各民族之间的缓冲，并执行现有国际条约。但像许多人那样论证，就是忘记联盟实际上是一个骗局，它不是其成员的机构，而是党的机构，一个完全从上面强加的结构，因此对几乎所有非俄罗斯居民和许多俄罗斯居民来说都是压迫工具。党一去，就没有任何力量——无论是军队、卢布，还是俄语这一通用语——能够维系联盟。叶利钦和民主派现实地接受了这一事实，不仅不抵制分离，而且实际上促成了联盟的拆除，甚至接受俄罗斯联邦本身的激进分权。这一看似冒险的策略背后的理由是，首先必须摧毁旧国家结构，以便后来俄罗斯联邦、可能还有联盟的某个邦联继承者，能够以真正民主的方式从下面重新构成自身。
en: On the surface it would seem plausible to preserve the political framework of the Union in some form in order to provide a unified economic space, to serve as a buffer among the nationalities, and to execute existing international treaties. But to argue in this way, as many have, is to forget that the Union was in fact a fraud, an agency not of its members but of the Party, a structure entirely imposed from above and as such an instrument of oppression to almost all its non-Russian and many of its Russian inhabitants. With the Party gone, there was no force—neither the army, nor the ruble, nor the

of the Russian language—capable of holding the Union together. Realistically accepting this fact, Yeltsin and the democrats not only refrained from resisting secession but indeed facilitated the dismantling of the Union and even accepted the radical decentralization of the Russian Federation itself. The rationale behind this seemingly risky strategy was that it was first necessary to destroy the old state structures so that later the Russian Federation, and possibly some confederal successor to the Union, might reconstitute themselves from below in authentically democratic fashion.

zh: 因此，八月革命之后，寻求新联盟条约已毫无意义。然而戈尔巴乔夫仍不断尝试，部分因为他确实忠于联盟，既出于实用，也出于民族伟大；部分也因为他需要有一个可以由他担任总统的国家。这种不合时宜的坚持也是对民主派的潜在政治威胁，实际上只助长了联盟的灭亡，因为到11月已清楚，只要旧国家还有一丝影子，这个对立的行政首脑就不会退休。
en: After the August Revolution, therefore, there was no longer any point in seeking a new Union Treaty. Still, Gorbachev kept trying, in part because he was genuinely committed to the Union, both as a matter of utility and as a matter of national grandeur, but in part also because he needed something to be president of. And this anachronistic persistence, which was also a potential political threat to the democrats, in fact only helped to doom the Union, since by November it had become clear that this rival executive would not retire so long as there existed a shadow of the old state.

zh: 但最终决定联盟命运的是叶利钦政府的激进经济选择。他回到500天计划的目标——市场化和私有化——即使没有回到其实现这些目标的具体条款。经过一番犹豫，10月底他选择更激进的“休克疗法”价格自由化政策，并任命叶戈尔·盖达尔为总理来实施。而且，如同500天计划一样，这一政策要求深远的共和国主权，作为分散经济权力以促进经济主动性的手段。然而，在八月革命之后和盖达尔任命之后，俄罗斯联邦比其它共和国更快地走向自由经济，而其他共和国则根本没有改革纲领。此外，俄罗斯联邦比大多数其他共和国更彻底地拆除了党国，后者旧党务机关和经济领域的任命制干部仍然掌权，尽管此时在民族旗帜之下。由于把俄罗斯休克疗法与这些共和国的保守主义拼在一起只会束缚改革，盖达尔的“少壮派”决心摆脱联盟。
en: But what finally sealed the Union’s fate was the radical economic choice of Yeltsin’s government. He returned to the goals of the 500-Day Plan—marketization and privatization—if not to its actual provisions for achieving them. After some hesitation, in late October he opted for a still more radical policy of “shock-therapy” price liberalization and appointed Yegor Gaidar prime minister to carry it out. And, as was the case with the 500-Day Plan, this policy entailed far-reaching republic sovereignty as a means of diffusing economic power to promote economic initiative. In the wake of the August Revolution and after Gaidar’s appointment, however, the Russian Federation was moving far more rapidly toward a liberal economy than were the other republics, which indeed had no program of reform at all. Moreover, the Russian Federation had dismantled the Party-state much more thoroughly than had most of the other republics, where the old Party apparat and economic

were still in power, though now under national flags. Since meshing Russian shock therapy with these republics’ conservatism would have only hobbled reform, Gaidar’s “Young Turks” became determined to cut free from the Union.

zh: 致命一击发生在12月，乌克兰以全民公决确认其议会早先的独立宣言，实际上终结了联盟。于是在叶利钦的推动下，三个斯拉夫共和国——俄罗斯、乌克兰和白俄罗斯——正式宣布联盟不复存在，并按照萨哈罗夫的一个旧想法，用一个松散的独立国家联合体取而代之。作为这一变化的一个预期副产品，戈尔巴乔夫别无选择，只能退休。
en: The coup de grâce came in December, when Ukraine confirmed its parliament’s earlier declaration of independence in a referendum, thereby in effect ending the Union. So at Yeltsin’s instigation the three Slavic republics—Russia, Ukraine, and Belorus—formally declared the Union to be defunct and replaced it, following an old idea of Sakharov’s, with a loose Commonwealth of Independent States. As an intended by-product of this change, Gorbachev was left with no choice but to retire.

zh: 于是，到1991年12月25日，当红旗最后一次在克里姆林宫降下，戈尔巴乔夫在电视上宣读告别演说时，苏联的关键机构已无一留存。1989年始于列宁主义在东欧崩溃的进程，现在以列宁主义在母国的崩溃而完成。正如一位俄罗斯评论家所说，苏联遭受了相当于在一场大战中战败的结构性后果。
en: Thus, by December 25, 1991, when the red flag came down over the Kremlin for the last time and Gorbachev read his farewell address over television, none of the key Soviet institutions remained. The process that had begun with the collapse of Leninism in Eastern Europe in 1989 was now completed with Leninism’s collapse in the mother country. As one Russian commentator put it, the Soviet Union had suffered the structural equivalent of defeat in a major war.

zh: 事实上，苏联的灾难更糟，因为它是自己造成的。俄罗斯帝国政权到1914年已处于深度衰朽，却仍经历了三年血腥战争，才在1917年2月解体。本世纪唯一可比的其他崩溃，即1945年轴心国和日本的崩溃，都是被毁灭性的军事失败造成的。但一个表面上先进的工业国家和超级大国，在没有大规模军事失败的情况下，在四十五年和平之后，基本上由于内部原因而崩溃，这在现代史上是闻所未闻的。
en: In fact, the Soviet catastrophe was worse, for it was self-inflicted. The Russian Imperial regime, which by 1914 was already in an advanced state of decay, nonetheless still had to undergo three years of bloody war before it fell apart in February 1917. And the only other comparable collapses in this century, those of the Axis and of Japan in 1945, were produced by crushing military defeat. But that an ostensibly advanced industrial nation and superpower should collapse without any large-scale military defeat, after forty-five years of peace, and essentially from internal causes, is unheard of in modern history.
